recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, $6.50M expiring, only 11 games against Aebischer's 19; the $6.50M is the largest single cash freed for the young-core locks and the crease is covered cheaply behind him.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign the balance of the 17-player expiring group on staggered 2-3 year deals, not 5-6.
recommendations.rationale: The 1y cluster is 17 players and $28.60M; putting only the four stars on long term and spreading the depth avoids the whole young core hitting the market in one summer.

recommendations.current: own round-0 pick and DET first-rounder
recommendations.summary: Hold the round-0 and the acquired Detroit first as ammunition; spend no more picks this season.
recommendations.rationale: The deadline already commits the R2, R3 and R4; keeping these two gives the GM a war chest for the summer renewals or one block-buster without over-paying.

recommendations.summary: Execute the three confirmed deadline deals before early March: Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flags toughness 70 and faceoffs 87 as the two holes. The package lifts toughness to 90/92 and faceoffs to 96 while cutting payroll by $2.56M. Terms are agreed; this is an execution calendar item.

recommendations.summary: Lock the five core players on 5-6 year deals in July.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 22 and $1.10M, Richards at 24 and $1.00M, Kaberle at 26 and $1.90M, Nash at 20 and $1.20M, Aebischer at 26 and $0.50M with .898 SV% in 19 starts. All cheap, all rising or prime. Five-year locks push their next negotiation past 2009 and break the 17-deal cluster.

recommendations.proposed: Holden, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Chistov, Alexeev, Upshall, Smirnov
recommendations.summary: Sign the seven young depth players on 2-3 year deals in July.
recommendations.rationale: All aged 20-26 on contracts under $1.20M. Two or three years is cheap insurance while we learn which of them are keepers. Staggered lengths so the next renewal wave is spread across 2006-2007 instead of all landing at once.

recommendations.summary: Let five contracts lapse in July: Svehla ($3.60M, 35), Roberts ($2.70M, 38), Renberg ($2.00M, 32), Belfour ($6.50M, 39), Tellqvist ($0.80M, 25).
recommendations.rationale: Frees $15.60M. Four veterans aged 32-39 on high salaries; Tellqvist at .865 SV% in seven games is not an option. If any veteran reads above 80 at the deadline, try to move him for a pick before letting him walk for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Keep Belfour through the playoffs, then plan the backup-goalie search for after July.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 10-1, .906, 3 SO in 11 starts. Tellqvist at .865 is not a playoff backup. Belfour walks in July at $6.50M and 39. The free-agent or trade search for Aebischer's backup starts in July, not in March.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Cammalleri (LA, 83 ovr, POTE 98, 22, $1.10M expiring) before the deadline or in summer; LA at 9-16-5 cannot keep him at market value.
recommendations.rationale: 83 overall at 22 with 98 potential on $1.10M from a 9-16-5 club is the best value in the league. He replaces Mogilny's wing scoring with five years of control at a fraction of the cost.

recommendations.summary: Belanger (LA, 78 ovr, FACE 96, 26, $0.70M expiring) is the insurance policy if the Sillinger deal collapses; LA at 9-16-5 will move him for a late pick.
recommendations.rationale: FACE 96 matches Sillinger at half the draft cost from a seller. One year rental at $0.70M is low risk even if we only use him through the playoffs.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, 80 ovr, 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 24, $0.90M, 2yr) is the deadline fallback if Jackman stalls; a mid-round pick prices him despite CHI's profitability.
recommendations.rationale: Two more years at $0.90M at age 24 makes him a better long-term fit than Jackman, but CHI's $25.12M profit reduces desperation. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Wanvig (MIN, 73 ovr, 87 TOUG, 88 CHKG, POTE 95, 23, $0.60M expiring) for a fourth-rounder fills the toughness gap on the wing if both Jackman and Bell stall.
recommendations.rationale: MIN at 12-22-1 with $32.57M profit have no incentive to keep a 73-overall expiring winger; POTE 95 makes him a re-sign candidate for next season.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, 77 ovr, FACE 94, 24, $0.40M, 2yr) is the cheapest faceoff depth available; bundle him with Cammalleri or Belanger in a multi-player LA package.
recommendations.rationale: $0.40M on two years with FACE 94 at 24 is the lowest-cost draw-winning depth in the league. Same club as Belanger and Cammalleri makes a package efficient.

recommendations.summary: Morrisonn (BOS, D, 73 ovr, POTE 99, 21, $1.10M expiring) is a summer target if Boston's 13-15-3 slides; a 99-potential D at $1.10M is the kind of asset that changes a blue line.
recommendations.rationale: Boston at 13-15-3 with $26.16M profit may not sell, but if January goes badly an expiring 21-year-old with POTE 99 is their only path to a return.

recommendations.summary: If the Sillinger deal is still being negotiated, ask PHX to bundle Taffe (74 ovr, POTE 97, 23, $0.40M expiring) into the same third-rounder; same club, same deal, no extra pick.
recommendations.rationale: Taffe is on PHX's expiring roster at $0.40M with POTE 97. They have no reason to keep him and no reason to demand a second pick for a fourth-liner.

recommendations.summary: Regehr (CGY, 68 ovr, 87 CHKG, 24, $1.26M, 3yr) stays the fallback for young checking on the blue line at third-rounder price from a 11-20-3 seller.
recommendations.rationale: 87 CHKG at 24 on three years fills the checking-age problem alongside Jackman; CGY at 11-20-3 with $11.56M profit have every reason to sell depth.

recommendations.current: Holden ($1.20M, C, 26, expiring, 0 GP) + DET round-1 pick
recommendations.summary: Offer LA Holden plus the Detroit first-round pick for Cammalleri, replacing Mogilny's scoring wing with a 22-year-old carrying 98 potential.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 9-16-5 will lose Cammalleri for nothing in July on an expiring deal. A first-rounder plus a 26-year-old centre on $1.20M is a rebuild-priced package. For Toronto, Cammalleri at 83 overall and POTE 98 fills the wing Mogilny vacates with five years of runway rather than six weeks of a rental. Payroll nets to minus $0.10M. Acceptance is uncertain; LA may want two picks or reject Holden as surplus.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick (round uncertain, above-80 expiring mechanic)
recommendations.summary: Move Belfour at the deadline to a contender for a draft pick using the above-80 expiring mechanic; his value evaporates in July.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour's $6.50M is the single largest contract on the roster and the biggest cash freed for the summer re-signing cluster of seventeen expiring deals. A contender with a shaky backup pays for a 0.906 SV veteran in a playoff run. The risk is Aebischer at 19 GP carrying the run with Tellqvist at 4.11 GAA as the third man. If the coach vetoes the goalie risk, re-sign Belfour on two years at a reduced number instead.

recommendations.summary: Flip Renberg for Belanger to pair a second 96-draw centre with Sundin and Sillinger without spending a pick.
recommendations.rationale: Renberg has 7 points in 12 games and is expiring on $2.00M; his ice is negligible. Belanger at FACE 96 alongside Sillinger at 96 and Sundin at 90 means the coach wins draws on three lines instead of one. LA at 9-16-5 sheds an expiring forward they cannot re-sign. Payroll nets to minus $1.30M. Only pursue this if the Cammalleri deal does not close the LA relationship first; bundling into one phone call with the same GM is cleaner.

recommendations.summary: If Cammalleri, Belfour and Belanger all fail, stop. The three confirmed deals close both coach-flagged gaps.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman (90 TOUG) and Sutton (92 TOUG) close toughness. Sillinger (FACE 96) closes faceoffs. The scoring wing drops to Gaborik, Afinogenov and Sundin, which is thin but survivable for a playoff run at 27-6-0. Spend nothing more at the deadline; preserve the DET first and TOR round-0 for the summer.

recommendations.summary: Line Tucker in a regular unit; he carries 83 CHKG and 70 TOUG and is currently not in any line.
recommendations.rationale: Lined checkers drop to three without him. The coach already proposed this swap on the PK. It is the only way to get a fourth 80+ checker into the lineup without a trade.

recommendations.summary: Confirm Jackman as the deadline toughness fix: 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, three years at $0.70M, from STL at 8-17-2.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players at 80+ toughness on this roster. No internal option closes it. Jackman is the only available target who does.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Sillinger at FACE 96 to share draws with Sundin; he is the best faceoff man available.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ faceoff man. Chlup at 75 is 18 and not a solution this season. Sundin at 33 cannot carry all four lines indefinitely.

recommendations.summary: Track Chlup's FACE development: he is 75 at 18 and the only internal path to a second 80+ faceoff man.
recommendations.rationale: If Sillinger is rented and not re-signed, the faceoff hole reopens. Chlup at 75 and climbing is the long-term answer, and the coach already wants him at 14+ minutes.

recommendations.summary: No action on scoring, playmaking, speed, stamina, or clutch roles this deadline.
recommendations.rationale: All five roles have multiple 80+ players with young cores (Gaborik 22, Afinogenov 25, Richards 24, Spacek 19). Spending picks here would be redundant.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal now, before the season's full production inflates his price above the $1.10M he carries today.
recommendations.rationale: 51 points in 34 games at 22 with 90 potential on a one-year deal worth $1.10M. Every game played before July raises the ask. This is the cheapest star contract the franchise will ever get.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on a 5-6 year deal alongside Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 34 games at 20, 95 potential, $1.20M, one year left. Same price-lock logic as Gaborik: current salary is well below what a full season at this rate will command.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on a 5-6 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 38 points in 34 games at 24, 88 potential, $1.00M with one year left. He is the third core player whose current salary is below market and whose value only rises with games played.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on a 5-6 year deal to anchor the blueline through the age transition.
recommendations.rationale: 18 points in 34 games at 26, $1.90M, one year left. He is the only defenceman combining current production with near-term prime. Without him the pairings are McCabe (29) plus prospects.

recommendations.current: Mattias Ohlund and remaining young depth
recommendations.proposed: 2-3 year deals on depth players expiring this summer
recommendations.summary: Sign the second tier of expiring young players (Colaiacovo, Chistov, Upshall, Alexeev, Eminger, Spacek, Spezza) on staggered 2-3 year deals after locking the four core players.
recommendations.rationale: 13 young players expire this summer at $15.7M combined. Locking four on 5-6 years and the rest on 2-3 staggers the renewal wave so no single summer carries the entire roster. Start with the core this week; depth follows by February.

recommendations.proposed: Keep through playoffs, then develop Aebischer or sign a free-agent backup
recommendations.summary: Plan the goalie transition: keep Belfour (39, $6.50M, CONS 50) through the playoffs, do not extend, and line up Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 90 POTE, 19 GP) as the 2005-06 starter with a veteran backup acquired in summer free agency.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour cannot be the answer in 2006 at 41. Trading him at the deadline for a pick loses the playoff goalie. Summer release or non-renewal at $6.50M saves the full contract and forces a development plan that Aebischer and Tellqvist can fill if given ice.

recommendations.summary: Hold the Detroit first-round pick through the deadline; do not spend it for a rental.
recommendations.rationale: It is the only premium asset on the board. The deadline targets (Jackman at R2 price, Sutton at R4 price) do not require it. Save it for a summer move or a deadline emergency in 2005.

recommendations.summary: Buy Jackman at the deadline for toughness: 83 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, three years at $0.70M, from a 8-17-2 St. Louis club that must shed.
recommendations.rationale: We are the 1st seed (56 pts) so the contending branch applies: buy for need with term. Jackman is the only 80-plus toughness option with term left and prices at a second-round pick.

recommendations.summary: Package Safronov plus a fourth-rounder for Sutton: 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 76 ovr, 27, $1.34M, four years.
recommendations.rationale: ATL are 8-18-2 rebuilding around Bouwmeester with no reason to keep a 27-year-old checking D; fills the D-side toughness hole the coach flagged.

recommendations.summary: Target Sillinger (FACE 96) as the deadline draw man behind Sundin; Conroy (FACE 93, CGY) is the fallback.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin at 87 clears 80 on the draw, so we lose it on three lines nightly; a near-second-round rental is worth two playoff rounds of possession.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny before the deadline as an above-80 asset we will not re-sign; prefer Mogilny to STL for Jackman plus the second-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: The coach has pulled him off the first line; 95 ovr on $5.5M prices him as a first-rounder via the mechanic, and his value falls after the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Keep Belfour (39, $6.5M expiring) as the Cup starter through the playoffs, then offer two years at $3.5-4M.
recommendations.rationale: He is the above-80 expiring mechanic candidate, but the manual says check the goalies and he is the playoff starter; reduce on term only after the run.

recommendations.summary: Lock the young core now on staggered 5-6 year deals: Gaborik (RW 22, $1.10M), Richards (C 24, $1.00M), Kaberle (D 26, $1.90M), Nash (LW 20, $1.20M).
recommendations.rationale: Stars renewed yearly only ratchet demands; staggered start dates break the same-summer $28.6M cluster.

recommendations.summary: Lock Colaiacovo (D 21, $1.10M) on a five-year deal while the money is cheap.
recommendations.rationale: A 21-year-old top-four blueliner at $1.10M is the cheapest future shutdown D we will ever get; pair with the Sutton buy as D depth.

recommendations.current: Upshall, Chistov, Smirnov, Eminger, Alexeev, Holden
recommendations.summary: Renew the young depth on 2-3 year deals at staggered terms so the $28.6M block never renews at once.
recommendations.rationale: These are the second wave of the expiring list; keeping them cheap and staggered holds the depth that wins cups.

recommendations.proposed: let go or move before expiry for a pick
recommendations.summary: Let go Svehla (D 35, $3.60M), Roberts (LW 38, $2.70M) and Renberg (LW 32, $2.00M); if any reads above 80 overall, move before expiry for a pick rather than lose him free.
recommendations.rationale: Ages 35, 38, 32 and $8.3M of expiring salary are the cull that funds the young-core locks; the above-80 mechanic recovers a pick instead of a free loss.

recommendations.proposed: multi-year deal for the Belfour successor
recommendations.summary: Renew one of Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) or Aebischer (26, $0.50M) on a real multi-year deal as the successor once Belfour is gone.
recommendations.rationale: The manual's check-the-goalies warning plus Belfour's expiry leaves the net unowned after next summer; consider a backup goalie at the deadline rather than trust an expiring two-deep.

recommendations.summary: Jackman (STL, 79 ovr, 87 CHKG, 86 TOUG, 90 POTE, 23, $0.70M, 3yr) for Mogilny plus a second-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: STL are 8-18-2 with $11.29M profit (thinnest among sellers) and nine expiring deals; they need a veteran scorer for the rebuild and Mogilny's 95 overall prices as first-round weight even at 35.

recommendations.summary: Regehr (CGY, 72 ovr, 91 CHKG, 82 TOUG, 24, $1.26M, 3yr) as the toughness-D fallback if Jackman stalls; third-rounder plus a depth forward.
recommendations.rationale: CGY are 9-20-3, worst in the West, with prestige 354 and zero playoff history; a nine-win team has no reason to keep a 24-year-old blueliner on three-year term when they can flip him for immediate help.

recommendations.summary: Sillinger (PHX, 88 ovr, FACE 96, 33, $1.80M, expiring) for a third-round pick; gives Sundin a draw partner on the second centre.
recommendations.rationale: PHX are 13-17-4 with 14 players expiring and no playoff path at 32 points; Sillinger's 27 points in 26 games and FACE 96 price as a second-round rental but the coach flagged the gap directly.

recommendations.summary: Conroy (CGY, 80 ovr, FACE 91, 33, $2.00M, expiring) as the faceoff fallback if Sillinger stalls; third-rounder only.
recommendations.rationale: CGY are 9-20-3 with 10 expiring deals; Conroy's 41 points in 34 games make him a better player than a pure draw man but the $2.0M expiring salary limits what Calgary will accept back.

recommendations.summary: Wanvig (MIN, 71 ovr, POTE 95, 86 CHKG, 85 TOUG, 23, $0.60M, expiring) for a late-round pick; fills toughness AND carries elite potential.
recommendations.rationale: MIN are 10-21-1 with $32.58M profit (highest in the league) but no reason to keep a 23-year-old on an expiring deal; his 85 TOUG closes the gap and POTE 95 means he is a keeper if he develops.

recommendations.summary: Belanger (LA, 72 ovr, FACE 90, 27, $0.70M, expiring) as the budget faceoff fix if both Sillinger and Conroy stall; sixth-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: LA are 8-15-5 with 13 expiring players; Belanger's 7 points in 33 games mark him as a pure draw man but FACE 90 at $0.70M is the cheapest available answer to the coach's flag.

recommendations.summary: Abid (PIT, 74 ovr, POTE 95, 83 CHKG, 83 TOUG, 24, $0.40M, expiring) for a fourth-rounder; cheap toughness with real upside.
recommendations.rationale: PIT are 9-16-5 with 14 expiring deals and $13.86M profit; his 39 points in 33 games show he can contribute beyond a checking role, making him a keeper candidate at $0.40M.

recommendations.summary: Chara is off the board: Ottawa at 12-13-4, 34 points, are holding 8th in the East and will not sell.
recommendations.rationale: The 2004-12-15 note confirmed Ottawa are inside the race; the Detroit-first package stays dead.

recommendations.summary: Send Mogilny and our second-round pick to STL for Jackman; payroll drops $4.80M and toughness goes from 73 to 90 with three years of term.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 8-18-2 need a veteran scorer around Bouwmeester and Mogilny's 95 overall and 44 points in 31 games still prices as first-round weight. They can flip Mogilny in July for more if it fails. The $5.50M salary is the risk: STL profit is only $11.29M, so acceptance on the money is uncertain.

recommendations.proposed: Mike Sillinger (PHX, 33, $1.80M, 1yr, FACE 96, 27 pts in 26 GP)
recommendations.summary: Trade our third-round pick to PHX for Sillinger's expiring deal; he gives Sundin a faceoff partner at 96 for the playoffs and clears from payroll in July.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 13-17-4 are eight out with 14 expiring contracts and are shedding in every direction. A R3 for a 33-year-old expiring rental is what sellers take. The only friction is whether their AI values 27 points in 26 games above a third-rounder.

recommendations.summary: Send Safronov and our fourth-round pick to ATL for Sutton; answers the coach's deadline question on Safronov, adds a 92-TOUG blueliner, and costs $0.44M net.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 8-18-2 are rebuilding around Bouwmeester with no reason to keep a 76-overall depth defenceman. Safronov at 23 with 91 POTE and a pick is upside they want. Safronov has played 3 games this season; he is surplus and the coach asked for a decision by the deadline.

recommendations.summary: If Jackman and Sutton both stall, target Wanvig at MIN for a fourth-rounder; he adds 85+ toughness with 95 potential on a cheap expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: MIN at 10-21-1 have the highest profit in the league at $32.58M, so they are not desperate, but a nine-win team has no use for a 23-year-old winger with 71 overall on an expiring deal. This is the emergency toughness add at minimal cost.

recommendations.summary: Do not spend the Detroit first-round pick before the summer; the three deadline deals above are priced at R2 and R4 level.
recommendations.rationale: The trajectory phase flags this pick as insurance for a summer star acquisition or a re-signing failure. Spending it at the deadline for a rental removes our only premium asset.

recommendations.summary: Move Nash from the third line to the second line tonight against STL.
recommendations.rationale: 0.91 points per game in 13 MPG at age 20 is the highest rate on the roster outside Gaborik. The top six is aging; he's the replacement in-house.

recommendations.summary: Give Chlup 14+ minutes a night, up from 11.8.
recommendations.rationale: 18 points in 22 games at 11.8 MPG as an 18-year-old is 0.82 per game. He's our only centre besides Sundin and his rate says he's ready for more.

recommendations.summary: Put Koltsov back in the lineup, bump Upshall to the press box.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov at 0.78 per game is nearly double Upshall's 0.41 per game. His production justifies a roster spot; Upshall's doesn't.

recommendations.summary: Name Safronov in or out of the plan before the trade deadline.
recommendations.rationale: 23 years old, 2 games, 12.5 MPG in each, zero points, 91 scouting number. The window to find out if he's a player closes by February.

recommendations.summary: Leave Spezza, Eminger and Smirnov as healthy scratches.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 0.48 per game and Eminger at 0.50 are not outproducing anyone in the lineup. Smirnov at 20 with zero games and the lowest ceiling is correctly outside the plan.

recommendations.summary: Give Chlup top-nine minutes; he is producing 1.11 pts/g at 13 MPG and has outgrown the fourth line.
recommendations.rationale: He went 0.62→1.11 pts/g while his ice climbed from 11.0 to 13.0. The GM's own standard is production over attribute weakness, and his scoresheet says second-line.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny off the first line; he is at 0.60 pts/g on 17.6 MPG and his rate is more than halved.
recommendations.rationale: He was 1.62 pts/g earlier in the season and is now producing at a fourth-line rate while occupying top-six minutes. The team cannot carry a 35-year-old at 0.60 on the first line while Chlup sits at 1.11 on the fourth.

recommendations.summary: Flag to GM: Koltsov at 23 has collapsed from 1.10 to 0.38 pts/g with ice down from 8.7 to 6.2; he needs a decision within two weeks.
recommendations.rationale: Both his rate and his minutes are falling simultaneously. At 23 this is the window where either a role is found or the plan moves on from him.

recommendations.summary: Watch Fischer's pairing: 0.63→0.22 pts/g while getting MORE ice (20.8→22.3). At 24, more ice with less production means the situation is wrong.
recommendations.rationale: This is not aging at 24. Either the defensive assignment has become too hard for him or his partner change removed a crutch. Try a different pairing before the next game.

recommendations.summary: Nash at 0.83→1.11 pts/g on flat minutes is exactly the trend you want; leave his role alone and let him keep climbing.
recommendations.rationale: He is producing more out of the same shift length. That is growth, not a problem to fix.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven lineup change before STL. The room is at 88 or above except Aebischer at 80, which minutes cannot fix.
recommendations.rationale: Morale range 80-100, average 92. Only Aebischer (18 GP, 57.8 MPG) is below 88, and as a goalie his minutes are games played, not something a line card adjusts. Everyone else is at or near their expected band with no slip that warrants action.

recommendations.slot: left wing on first penalty kill
recommendations.summary: Swap Mogilny off the first penalty kill for Tucker, who carries 79 checking and 68 toughness versus Mogilny's contribution as a 35-year-old winger.
recommendations.rationale: K1 checking mean drops to 71 with Mogilny on it. Tucker is at 79 checking and 68 toughness and currently scratched. This is a one-player swap on a four-man unit; chemistry cost is minimal since PK assignments shift frequently.

recommendations.summary: L1 and L2 are built correctly for their assignments; leave them intact.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has three 80+ checkers protecting Mogilny and Sundin at faceoffs (87). L2 is our deepest scoring line (Gaborik 97, Afinogenov 90) and breaking it to add a checker costs more than the faceoff loss saves. No swap improves either unit.

recommendations.summary: L4's 52 mean faceoffs and 64 mean checking are a roster gap I cannot fix with bodies on hand.
recommendations.rationale: No available player combines faceoffs above 70 with checking above 80. Upshall is the best checker on L4 at 81 but cannot take draws. This remains the same structural gap flagged December 7th.

recommendations.summary: Only Sundin (87) wins faceoffs above 80; Chlup is next at 76. We lose the draw on three lines every game.
recommendations.rationale: This forces our defencemen into coverage they shouldn't face. No arrangement of existing personnel fixes it. A centre with 80+ faceoffs is the single highest-impact addition available to us.

recommendations.summary: Best toughness on the roster is 70 (McCabe). We have no enforcer and no shutdown option beyond the first line.
recommendations.rationale: Against a physical team in a playoff series, we have no answer. Tucker at 68 toughness is the next best and he's a depth checker, not an enforcer. This remains unsolvable from within the lineup.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour in net against STL.
recommendations.rationale: Aebischer is at 80 morale, the lowest on the roster. Belfour is 91 OVR with 95 morale, and this is an 8-17-2 team with a 10 percent power play and a goalie at 81. No result risk in resting Aebischer here.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for STL.
recommendations.rationale: We outclass them at every position. Their physical players (Walker, McCarthy) are third and fourth liners our young guys can handle. The faceoff matchup actually favors us tonight with Weight at 74 versus Sundin at 87.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jackman (90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 83 ovr, 23, $0.70M, three years) via Mogilny-plus-second package to fill the roster's only zero-depth role.
recommendations.rationale: No player on TOR carries 80+ toughness. The ceiling is 73. Jackman at 90 TOUG and 91 CHKG, three years of term at $0.70M, is the only player who turns this role from missing to covered. STL at 8-17-2 need scoring help and Mogilny at 95 ovr/42 pts in 28 GP is their solution.

recommendations.summary: Acquire a second faceoff centre (FACE 93+) at the deadline to relieve Sundin's 22-minute draw duty.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (FACE 90) is above 80 on the roster. Chlup at 75, Richards at 70, Holden at 71. A playoff team needs a centre who wins the draw against opposing top lines. Sillinger (96) and Conroy (93) are second-round-priced rentals that close this without long-term cap cost.

recommendations.summary: Line Koltsov at third-line LW to put the team's fifth-fastest skater (92 SPEE) into the lineup and reduce top-pair load.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov at 92 speed is on the roster and in no unit. The coach already flagged this move. It distributes speed across three lines instead of concentrating it on the top two with Mogilny (35) and Sundin (33).

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly for his 83 CHKG and 70 TOUG to lift the checking group from four to five usable bodies.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is 83 CHKG (tied for third on the roster) and not lined. Fischer is 82 CHKG at 24. Both should be dressed. The coach's report already flags Tucker as the internal floor if no toughness target lands.

recommendations.summary: Line Salo (88 scoring, 30) into a nightly role; he is the team's fifth-best scorer and currently not in any unit.
recommendations.rationale: Salo at 88 is above four players the coach is using. At 30 he is not a development case; he is a productive winger on the bench. Either he plays or he becomes trade bait for the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour before the deadline for a pick using the above-80 expiring asset mechanic, or commit to keeping him through playoffs and re-sign at $3.5-4M on two years.
recommendations.rationale: 39, $6.50M, 1y, CONS 50, 10 GP. Value only drops after the deadline. Either extract something or plan the reduced re-sign now.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup (18, 2y remaining, 95 POTE) to a 5-6 year deal this season to get five more years of control before UFCA at 20.
recommendations.rationale: Two years remaining means he hits UFCA at 20. An extension now costs a small salary bump and prevents a second $2.34M+ re-up at 22. Same logic applies to Nash (20, 1y, 95 POTE) and Gaborik (22, 1y, 47 pts).

recommendations.proposed: extend one at low cost before expiry
recommendations.summary: Tellqvist (25, $0.80M, 1y) and Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 1y) both expire the same summer Belfour does. Extend one at current rate before they leave for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Three goalies on one-year deals is a coverage gap. A $0.80M extension on Tellqvist costs almost nothing now and prevents a free-agent search behind a 39-year-old or a rookie.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jackman from St. Louis for a second-round pick within three weeks; by March STL may re-sign or reprice.
recommendations.rationale: STL are 8-17-2 and financially pressed, forcing a sell. Jackman is 23 with three years left at $0.70M — this is the toughness buy, not a rental. Execute before STL's record changes the AI's evaluation.

recommendations.proposed: a first-round pick or young package from STL or VAN
recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny before the deadline; his above-80 value is falling every week he is scratched.
recommendations.rationale: 95 overall prices as first-round weight via the above-80 mechanic, but at 35 and 0.75 pts/GP on $5.50M with two years left, every week costs us. If STL want Jackman plus Mogilny as a package back, that nets the toughness swap and clears $4.80M.

recommendations.current: Safronov (TOR, D, morale sliding toward 80s, 31 dressed scratches)
recommendations.proposed: a late-round pick or high-potential depth defenceman
recommendations.summary: Trade Safronov by mid-February while morale and trade value are still above 80; after that both fall.
recommendations.rationale: Coach reports him scratched 31 times with morale sliding. His value is time-sensitive: once morale hits the 80s the grade modifier takes 2 points and a suitor's asking price drops.

recommendations.proposed: a late-round pick or a prospect
recommendations.summary: Move Holden before the deadline; do not let him walk in July for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: At 26 with one year left he is the fourth-line centre a contender would take. Moving him yields an asset; letting him expire yields nothing.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal before season end; do not wait for free agency.
recommendations.rationale: He is the team's best young forward at 22. Yearly re-signing ratchets his demands per the manual. Lock him now at a modest raise on $1.10M.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards to a 5-6 year deal; franchise centre at 24 on $1.00M cannot be left to yearly renewals.
recommendations.rationale: Same logic as Gaborik. $1.00M at 24 is below market; a 5-year lock at $2.5-3.0M is still cheap against what the market will pay a 24-year-old centre.

recommendations.summary: Lock Kaberle to a 5-year deal; prime-age top-pairing defenceman, the one D we must retain.
recommendations.rationale: At 26 and $1.90M he is entering his prime. Losing him and retaining only Eminger and Colaiacovo would leave the blue line two years too young.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash on a 5-6 year deal; 20-year-old with 85 TOUG and 80 CHKG already dressing on line 3.
recommendations.rationale: Our only internal supply of toughness. At 20 and $1.20M, a 5-year lock at $1.5-2.0M is insurance against having to buy toughness on the market every year.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger on a 4-5 year deal; Coach says protect his rising role and his pairing.
recommendations.rationale: He is the young D whose role is growing. Four or five years keeps him with the core without the 6-year cost of a star lock.

recommendations.summary: Lock Colaiacovo on a 4-year deal or move him; do not let him develop by accident into an unrestricted asset.
recommendations.rationale: Three young D's (Eminger, Colaiacovo, Svehla-expiring) means we need to name two as keepers. Eminger and Colaiacovo are the pair.

recommendations.summary: Renew Alexeev on 2-3 years; his 2C promotion is a trial, not yet earned a longer deal.
recommendations.rationale: If he produces at 2C we extend to four or five years later. Signing him long now prices on potential we have not yet confirmed.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov on 2-3 years at a modest raise; fourth-line depth, cheap to retain.
recommendations.rationale: At 21 and $1.10M he is cheap. Two years keeps him in the system without a long commitment on a fourth-liner.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall on 2 years; young wing depth at $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: Depth player at 21. Two years costs little and preserves the roster shape.

recommendations.summary: Renew Smirnov on 2 years at $0.40M; at that price he is free to retain.
recommendations.rationale: Coach says name him in or out. At $400K the answer is in; he costs nothing and at 20 he has two years of development runway.

recommendations.proposed: sign one to a 3-year deal as the successor to Belfour; let the other walk
recommendations.summary: Decide by April which of Tellqvist or Aebischer is the future starter and sign him to three years; the other leaves.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39 and done. Two young goalies expiring means we lose both in July if we wait. The manual warns: check the goalies.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Belfour. His game is over at 39 on $6.50M with CONS 50.
recommendations.rationale: No player at 39 with a 50 consistency grade is worth $6.50M on a contender. Move him before March if possible via the above-80 mechanic; otherwise let him walk in July.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Svehla, Roberts or Renberg. Combined they are $8.30M of expiring money for players 32-38.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla at 35, Roberts at 38 on 22-minute loads, Renberg replacement-level at $2.00M. None fits the 5-veteran target shape. Svehla: move before deadline if above 80.

recommendations.summary: Do not buy at the deadline beyond Jackman. We are 8 points clear of second; additional rental cost or prospect drain is not justified by the regular season we have already won.
recommendations.rationale: 54 points in 31 games with the East lead by 8. The playoff seeding is secure. The only deadline acquisition that matters is Jackman, which improves the roster for June as well as April.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Sutton: 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 76 ovr, 27, $1.34M, four years, from ATL who are 8-18-2 and rebuilding. Fills the defenceman-with-toughness gap the roster has no answer for.
recommendations.rationale: Sutton is the only defenceman on a selling club carrying 90+ TOUG and 85+ CHKG under age 30. ATL have 11 expiring deals and no reason to keep a 76-overall D while rebuilding around Bouwmeester (78, 21, same club). Four years of control at $1.34M is the cheapest term-adjusted value on the board.

recommendations.summary: Jackman remains the primary toughness buy: 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 83 ovr, 23, $0.70M, three years from STL at 8-17-2 who must shed their $56.63M payroll.
recommendations.rationale: STL have the second-highest payroll in the league and the sixth-worst record. Mogilny plus a second-round pick gives them a 95-overall scorer they lack and the pick they need for their rebuild. No other club on the board offers 90+ TOUG and 91 CHKG at 23 on three cheap years.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sillinger as a deadline rental for the faceoff gap: 96 FACE, 88 ovr, 33, $1.80M, one year, from PHX who are 12-16-4 and out of the race.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 FACE is the only Toronto centre above 80 and he carries 22-minute loads. Sillinger's 96 FACE and 88 overall make him a top-six contributor who wins draws in the spring without a long-term commitment. PHX are 12-16-4 with 14 expiring contracts; a second-round pick prices correctly for a one-year rental at $1.80M.

recommendations.summary: Bell is the toughness fallback if Jackman stalls: 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 85 FACE, 80 ovr, 24, $0.90M, two years.
recommendations.rationale: Already known. CHI are 6-18-6 but profitable at $22.88M, so they are not financially forced to sell. Bell at 24 with two years left is a rebuild piece they may want to keep. Only pursue if STL reject the Jackman package.

recommendations.summary: Conroy is the faceoff fallback if Sillinger stalls: 91 FACE, 80 ovr, 33, $2.00M, one year, from CGY at 9-20-2 who are the most desperate sellers in the league.
recommendations.rationale: CGY have 10 expiring contracts, the second-worst record, and $13.15M profit that says they can absorb a loss on salary. At 33 and expiring he is a pure rental like Sillinger but at 91 FACE rather than 96. Same second-round pricing band.

recommendations.summary: Miller is the goalie solution for the summer: 81 ovr, 95 potential, 24, $1.00M, expiring, from BUF at 11-14-2 who are out of the race.
recommendations.rationale: All three Toronto goalies walk this summer. Miller at 81 and 95 potential with term expiring is the above-80 asset the market mechanic prices well. BUF have $18.60M profit and no urgency, but an expiring 81-giveaway for a first-round pick is clean for both sides. The DET first is the offer.

recommendations.summary: Name Cammalleri but do not bid at the deadline: 79 ovr, 97 potential, 22, $1.10M, from LA at 8-14-5 who are rebuilding.
recommendations.rationale: A 22-year-old with 97 potential at 79 overall is the kind of player the manual's depth-wins principle is built around. But LA are rebuilding and will demand the DET first, which is better spent on Jackman or Miller. Track him for the summer.

recommendations.current: Mogilny (RW, 95 ovr, 42 pts/28 GP, $5.50M, 2yr) + R2 pick (TOR)
recommendations.summary: Send Mogilny plus the TOR second-rounder to STL for Jackman; net payroll drops $4.80M and toughness goes from 73 to 90.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 8-17-2 with $56.63M payroll and $12.00M profit must shed; Mogilny gives them a 95-overall scorer for two years while their young core develops. Their profit drops to ~$7.20M, which is tight. Acceptance is uncertain — if they balk at $5.50M for two years, fall back to R2-only or Bell from CHI.

recommendations.summary: Send the TOR third-rounder to PHX for Sillinger as a deadline rental; the 96 FACE draw wins solve the gap behind Sundin for the spring.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 12-16-4 are out of the race and Sillinger is expiring at $1.80M; a third-round pick is fair value for a rental. We add $1.80M for one season. We currently have only Sundin (90) above 80 FACE and he is on 22-minute loads.

recommendations.current: Safronov (D, 74 ovr, 91 POTE, 23, $0.90M, 3yr, morale sliding) + R4 pick (TOR)
recommendations.summary: Package Safronov plus the TOR fourth-rounder to ATL for Sutton; fills the D-side toughness gap and resolves the coach's Safronov decision before his value erodes further.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 8-18-2 are rebuilding around Bouwmeester and Sutton at 76 is outside their core. Safronov at 23 with 91 potential fits their timeline. The coach has flagged Safronov's 31st dressed scratch and says his morale is sliding toward the 80s; his trade value is time-sensitive. Net payroll is +$0.44M.

recommendations.summary: Move Koltsov up to third-line left wing, Chistov to fourth.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov has 14 points in 18 games at 7.6 MPG (0.78/game). Chistov has 7 points in 18 games at 10.2 MPG (0.39/game). Koltsov is producing double the rate on a third fewer minutes.

recommendations.summary: Move Alexeev to second-line centre where his production can impact wins.
recommendations.rationale: 19 points in 32 games at 10.0 MPG. He is producing at top-six rates while sitting on the fourth line every night.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a fixed fourth-line centre role rather than rotating him.
recommendations.rationale: 14 points in 29 games at 8.3 MPG shows he's productive but the low minutes suggest rotation. A fixed role at 21 lets him build chemistry and grow into the position. His morale at 88 is also the second-lowest of the young group.

recommendations.summary: Safronov needs to be named in or out of the plan before the trade deadline.
recommendations.rationale: 23 years old, 1 game played, 0 points, POTE 91. He is not developing because he is not playing, and nobody has decided what he is.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov is not earning a roster spot and should not be pushed for one.
recommendations.rationale: 0 games, 0 points, POTE 70. The GM set production as the measure. There is nothing to point at yet.

recommendations.summary: No line change for Chlup despite his morale reading of 82.
recommendations.rationale: 17 points in 21 games at 11.8 MPG is good for an 18-year-old third-line centre. Morale at 82 warrants watching but the production says his role is correct.

recommendations.summary: Give Chlup top-six centre minutes now, not next season.
recommendations.rationale: He's 18 at 1.12 points a game in his last 8 (13 games to 21) while his ice only moved 11.0 to 13.0; his rate earns a bigger role.

recommendations.summary: Keep Eminger's rising role and ice, don't break his pairing.
recommendations.rationale: He jumped 0.35 to 1.00 a game with minutes up 15.0 to 20.0 across the window; that's a defenceman taking a step we should feed.

recommendations.summary: Cut Koltsov to a reduced role until his production returns.
recommendations.rationale: He fell from 1.10 to 0.38 a game and his ice to 6.2; by the GM's own rule that's production losing him the job, not the weaknesses on paper.

recommendations.summary: Name Smirnov and Safronov in or out of the plan; right now they're developing by accident.
recommendations.rationale: Smirnov is 20 with zero games this window and Safronov has 1 game at 23; default is not a plan.

recommendations.summary: Begin planning the top six without Mogilny's current pace.
recommendations.rationale: He's 0.75 a game against 1.62 to start the year at 35, on more ice, not less; the fade is real and the line must not depend on it.

recommendations.summary: Watch the 22-minute loads on Sundin and Roberts and find a fourth option to relieve them.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 38 went 16.5 to 22.0 minutes while slipping to 1.12; Sundin at 33 is 1.12 on 21.4. More ice, less rate, at their ages.

recommendations.summary: Dress Safronov tonight on the third defensive pair and give him real minutes to stop his morale slide before it reaches the 80s.
recommendations.rationale: He dropped 5 in one save (100 to 95) with 1 game played in 32. At that rate he'll be in the 70s within two weeks, costing 2 points on every grade. He is 23 with a 91 scouting number and needs to either play or go.

recommendations.summary: GM decision needed: Safronov is a dressed scratch for the 31st time. If he's not in the plan, trade him now while his morale (and trade value) is high.
recommendations.rationale: One game in 32 with morale falling 5 per save means he will be a problem within a month. The earlier finding that this is a decision being made by default is now confirmed by the morale data.

recommendations.summary: No line changes needed for morale reasons tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Every other player is at 82 or above with no movement that demands intervention. Chlup at 82 is producing at 0.81 pts/game on 11.8 minutes and his floor is the team record. Aebischer at 80 already has the most starts.

recommendations.summary: All four lines and both special teams are correctly built for this roster. No change before TB.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has scoring, checking and the draw. L2 is a possession line with 80 playmaking but only 62 checking mean — no alternative body exists that fixes that. L3 is developing (59 clutch). PP and PK units are balanced. Restructuring breaks chemistry for no grade improvement.

recommendations.slot: second-line left wing or third-line centre
recommendations.summary: We need one more body with 80+ checking and ideally 75+ faceoffs. Tucker at 78 is the only option and he is not in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe 81, Fischer 81, Roberts 80 are the only checkers above 78 and all play on L1 or K1. L2 checking mean is 62. Against a physical team we have no second shutdown unit. Faceoffs beyond Sundin (88) and Chlup (75) top out at Richards (72).

recommendations.summary: L3's clutch of 59 and stamina of 59 confirm it is a development line. Give them low-danger minutes and let them grow.
recommendations.rationale: The unit has speed (83 mean) and one player with 95 scoring. The weakness is experience, not attributes. Chlup at 75 faceoffs is the second-best on the roster and he is doing the job asked of him.

recommendations.summary: Play the existing lines as they are. TB's thin defence and weak top-centre faceoff reward our current structure without adjustment.
recommendations.rationale: TB's best D is Boyle at 75; after that everyone is 65-70. Lecavalier's FACE is 60, so Sundin at 88 wins the L1 draw and feeds our top line offensive zone time against their weakest group. TB is not physical enough to test our toughness gap. No matchup reason to alter anything.

recommendations.summary: Start Aebischer (84) over Tellqvist (73).
recommendations.rationale: TB's top six has 90+ speed (St. Louis 90, Lecavalier 91). Aebischer's 86 speed handles their transition; Tellqvist is at 76 and 11 points behind overall. Khabibulin on their side at 86 means we need our best net.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jackman at the deadline: zero players at 80+ TOUG on the roster, he carries 90 TOUG and 91 CHKG at 23 on three years and $0.70M.
recommendations.rationale: The toughness role has no internal solution; Tucker's 70 TOUG is the ceiling of what is already here. St. Louis are 7-16-2 and financially pressed. A second-round pick is the price.

recommendations.summary: Rent a faceoff centre who wins draws at 90+ to pair alongside Sundin, freeing him from a 60-point load.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (FACE 90) can win a draw. Chlup's 75 is the next best and he is 18. A second-round pick for a rental is the cost; acceptance is uncertain but both clubs are sellable.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly; his 83 CHKG makes him the fourth-best checker on the roster and he is the only internal addition to the checking role.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is on the roster, lined nowhere, at $1.30M and 29. Fischer at 24 carries 82 CHKG but should grow into the third-pairing role rather than absorb every shift Tucker can take.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, playmaking, speed and clutch are all covered by 80+ depth; no external acquisition needed in those roles.
recommendations.rationale: 13 at 80+ scoring, 25 at 80+ speed, 8 at 80+ clutch. Mogilny at 94 not lined is a trade asset decision, not a gap.

recommendations.summary: Belfour at 39, $6.50M expiring, SV 0.907: keep through the playoffs, then use the above-80 expiring mechanic to trade for a pick or re-sign at a reduced two-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: Aebischer is covered at 26 and GAA 2.76. Tellqvist at GAA 4.11 is not an NHL backup. Belfour's contract year makes him a trade candidate at the deadline or in June regardless.

recommendations.proposed: Nash, Gaborik, Richards, Colaiacovo on 5-6 year deals
recommendations.summary: Lock the four highest-value young players on long deals this summer at or near their current salary to break the 17-contract cluster.
recommendations.rationale: All four carry one year left, POTE 90-99, and are producing (Nash 28 pts/32 GP, Gaborik 44 pts/32 GP, Richards 33 pts/32 GP, Colaiacovo 8 pts/17 GP). Signing them at $1.10-1.20M on 5-6 years staggers the renewals and removes the risk of losing them to the same summer.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny before the deadline while he still prices as a first-round asset.
recommendations.rationale: 35 years old, 2 years left at $5.50M, 42 points in 28 games but scratched, POTE 55. His value only declines after the deadline. A contending club pays for 42 points in 28 games regardless of age.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour at the deadline using the above-80 expiring asset mechanic for a pick or young goalie.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50, 10 GP. The above-80 expiring asset rule means any contender gives something for him. Keeps the goaltending transition clean and frees $6.50M for Aebischer or Tellqvist at a lower rate.

recommendations.summary: Let Svehla, Roberts and Renberg walk at season's end rather than re-signing 32-38 year olds on short deals that recreate the cluster.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 35, scratched, $3.60M. Roberts is 38, POTE 52, $2.70M. Renberg is 32, 12 GP, $2.00M. Together $8.30M that can fund the young-core extensions without creating a second 17-contract summer in 2006.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jackman at the deadline for a second-round pick; 83 overall, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, three years at $0.70M.
recommendations.rationale: Fixes the toughness gap the coach flagged (best on roster is 70) and he is 23 with three years of control. STL at 7-16-2 must shed.

recommendations.summary: Buy a faceoff-winning centre at the deadline for a second-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 86 FACE is the only 80-plus draw man; Sillinger has 96 FACE, Conroy 93. We lose the draw on three lines every game.

recommendations.summary: Sell Mogilny before the deadline; 95 overall, $5.50M, 0.75 pts/game, scratched.
recommendations.rationale: Above-80 expiring-adjacent asset. The pick mechanic works now; value falls after the deadline. Frees $5.50M.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik (22, $1.10M) on a five- or six-year deal the day free agency opens.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest star in the league at his age and salary. Star deals on 5-6 years per the manual; yearly ratchets demands.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards (24, $1.00M) on a five- or six-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: Core centre behind Sundin at 24 and $1.00M. Star-length deal.

recommendations.summary: Lock Kaberle (26, $1.90M) on a five-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: Top-pairing offensive D at 26. Core lock.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash (20, $1.20M, 80 overall, 85 TOUG) on a five- or six-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: Internal toughness floor, already dressed on line 3 at 20. Lock him before his price rises.

recommendations.current: Upshall, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Chistov, Alexeev, Holden
recommendations.summary: Renew the six young depth players on two- or three-year deals to stagger the cluster.
recommendations.rationale: Locking all on five years recreates the same summer they all come up together. Two-to-three years staggers the wall.

recommendations.summary: Let Svehla go. Do not re-sign a 35-year-old at $3.60M.
recommendations.rationale: That salary belongs to a 24-year-old. At 35 with one year left, the value is gone.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts go. If above 80 overall, move him at the deadline for a pick.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, $2.70M, and his toughness of 70 is the best grade on our roster. The roster is past him.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) on two years as the succession plan behind Belfour.
recommendations.rationale: The manual says check the goalies. Belfour at 39 and CONS 50 means the next man is needed now.

recommendations.proposed: 2 year extension at $3.50-4.00M, or let walk
recommendations.summary: After the playoffs, offer Belfour two years at $3.50-4.00M reduced, or let him walk.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, $6.50M, CONS 50. Keep through the post-season; the reduced two-year deal or a walk is the right answer after.

recommendations.summary: Release Smirnov. He is not owed a roster spot.
recommendations.rationale: Zero games at 20, POTE 70, and the coach flagged him explicitly. $0.40M is nothing but the spot is real.

recommendations.summary: Trade a second-round pick to St. Louis for Jackman: 83 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, $0.70M, three years left, 31.9 minutes a night.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto have zero players at 80+ TOUG. Jackman is the only live target combining elite toughness, youth, cost and term. STL are 8-17-2 with $56.63M payroll and nine expiring contracts; they need to shed. Acceptance is uncertain but the fit is clean.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sillinger from PHX for a draft pick: 96 FACE, 88 ovr, 27 pts in 26 GP, $1.80M expiring. PHX are 12-16-4 with 14 expiring contracts.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at FACE 90 is the only 80+ option; Chlup at 75 is 18. Sillinger wins the draw on two more lines. PHX are out of the race and have no reason to keep a 33-year-old centre on an expiring deal.

recommendations.summary: If PHX holds Sillinger, pivot to Conroy: 93 FACE, 82 ovr, 36 pts in 32 GP, $2.00M expiring from CGY at 9-20-2.
recommendations.rationale: Same role as Sillinger at similar age and contract. CGY have 10 expiring contracts and the second-worst record in the league. A rental faceoff centre is worth a second-round pick to a 24-6-0 club.

recommendations.summary: Explore Bell from CHI: 80 ovr, 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 24, $0.90M, two years left. CHI are 6-18-6.
recommendations.rationale: Cheaper and younger than Jackman at a lower overall. CHI have $22.88M profit so they are not desperate, but 6-18-6 creates pressure to re-tool. If Jackman falls through, Bell is the fallback toughness target at a lower price.

recommendations.summary: Offer the DET first-round pick to LA for Cammalleri: 83 ovr, 98 POTE, 22, $1.10M expiring. LA are 8-14-5 with 13 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: The highest-potential player available at the deadline. 98 POTE at 22 for a first-round pick is a keeper, not a rental. If the GM values the long-term roster over a faceoff rental, this is the better use of the pick.

recommendations.summary: Take Abid from PIT for a third-round pick: 78 ovr, 95 POTE, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 24, $0.40M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Budget depth with real toughness and high potential at 24. PIT are 9-14-5 with 14 expiring contracts. Fills the fourth line and gives the coach a body who can finish a check without costing a second-round pick.

recommendations.summary: Take Komisarek from MTL for a third or conditional second: 80 ovr, 83 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 90 POTE, 22, $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: MTL are 9-19-2 with 14 expiring contracts. At 22 with 90 potential and 83/90 toughness and checking, he is blue-line depth who can play third-pair minutes tonight and grow into more.

recommendations.summary: Use Mogilny's 95 ovr above-80 expiring status to collect a draft pick rather than benching a $5.50M player.
recommendations.rationale: The game mechanic moves any above-80 player the AI does not intend to re-sign for a draft pick. Mogilny has two years left and Toronto will not re-sign him at $5.50M at 35. His trade value only falls after the deadline.

recommendations.current: Mogilny (RW, 35, 95 ovr, $5.50M, 2 yrs, 42 pts/28 GP) + TOR 2nd-round pick
recommendations.summary: Send Mogilny and the TOR second to St. Louis for Jackman; net payroll drop of $4.80M and the toughness gap closes from 0 players at 80+ TOUG to one at 90.
recommendations.rationale: STL are 8-17-2, $56.63M payroll, $12.00M profit, 9 expiring deals: they are shedding and Mogilny at 95 ovr with 1.50 pts/game gives them a veteran scorer for the rebuild. Acceptance is uncertain because $5.50M on their books is a stretch and Jackman at 23 with 3 years cheap is a core piece they may keep.

recommendations.current: Holden (C, 26, $1.20M, 1 yr, 0 GP, not dressed) + DET 1st-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Sillinger (C, 27, 88 ovr, FACE 96, 27 pts/26 GP, $1.80M, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Send Holden and the DET first to Phoenix for Sillinger; the FACE 96 wins draws on two lines and closes the coach's three-line faceoff deficit for $1.80M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: PHX are 12-16-4 with 14 expiring contracts and want to clear $1.80M; a first-round pick is strong currency at that record. Acceptance is uncertain because Phoenix may demand a young player instead of a 0-GP forward.

recommendations.proposed: Conroy (C, 33, 82 ovr, FACE 93, 36 pts/32 GP, $2.00M, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Fallback if Phoenix won't move Sillinger: send the same Holden-plus-DET-first package to Calgary, who are 9-20-2 and more desperate to shed.
recommendations.rationale: CGY have 10 expiring contracts and the second-worst record; a first-round pick plus a $1.20M body clears Conroy's $2.00M. FACE 93 is 3 points below Sillinger but 36 points in 32 games is more production.

recommendations.summary: If none of the three trade proposals land, dress Tucker nightly (CHKG 92, TOUG 88, $1.30M, only 3 GP so far) and promote Chlup to second-line draws; accept FACE 75 on two lines and re-attack toughness and faceoffs in summer free agency.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's internal fixes are Tucker on checking and Chlup on draws, but neither gets above 88 TOUG or 75 FACE. This is a playoff compromise, not a fix.

recommendations.summary: Bump Koltsov's minutes from 8.0 to 10 or 11; he's producing at 0.82 pts/game, the best rate per minute on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 14 points in 17 games at 8.0 minutes is a better production rate than any other young player on the list. POTE 94 and the rate say he's ready for the 10-minute band he's sitting just below.

recommendations.summary: Dress Colaiacovo in more games; 52% share is inconsistent with the 17.5 minutes he gets when he's in.
recommendations.rationale: 17.5 MPG when dressed says the staff trusts him with the puck; 52% share says they don't trust him with every game. POTE 99 at 21. The contradiction should resolve toward more games, not fewer minutes.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 8.6 minutes is the lowest MPG of any dressed young player; POTE 99 says that should not be the case.
recommendations.rationale: 14 points in 28 games at 8.6 minutes is a 0.50 pts/game rate, which is fine but the minutes are low for a 99-POTE player at 21. The production doesn't demand the third line yet, but the fourth line should not be this small a look.

recommendations.summary: Safronov is 23 with zero games and POTE 91; the GM needs to name him in or out of the plan.
recommendations.rationale: This has been flagged since December 15th and is still unresolved. A 91 scouting number at 23 with no games played is a decision being made by default, and the window is not infinite.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at 19 with POTE 70, zero games, and a scratch is not owed a roster spot.
