recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 38 at $2.7M, Renberg 32, Smirnov 50 ovr with 70 potential; Svehla plays the run then walks at 35, $3.6M.

recommendations.summary: Keep Belfour through the playoffs, then offer two years at about $3.5M.
recommendations.rationale: 91 ovr, 39, $6.5M expiring — the reduced term is the offer; if he balks, Aebischer owns the net.

recommendations.summary: Trade Detroit's first and Holden for Chara now; he is the toughness fix the roster lacks.
recommendations.rationale: Chara is 84 ovr with 92 TOUG and 93 CHKG at 27 and $1.7M expiring, against a Toronto roster whose best toughness is Roberts at 73. Ottawa at 29 points with 11 expiring deals has no reason to keep him; we take on $1.7M that clears this summer.

recommendations.summary: If Chara falls through, trade the second-round pick for Jackman, the toughness fix that stays three years.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman is 83 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, at $0.7M for three years, and St. Louis at 22 points sells. Costs a second instead of a first and is under contract past this spring.

recommendations.summary: If Vancouver sells, move Mogilny and our first for Bertuzzi: 95 ovr and 89 TOUG, and the payroll sheet improves by $2.9M.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is 35 with two years at $5.5M and his scoring fell from 1.62 to 0.75 a game while minutes rose; 42 points still reads as a scorer, so now is the window to cash him. Bertuzzi is expiring at $2.6M, but Vancouver at .620 may keep him, so take the deal only if it opens.

recommendations.summary: Give Koltsov more ice — he has earned it.
recommendations.rationale: 13 points in 15 games at 8.6 minutes and just 52% of games is a man outproducing his role; the scoresheet, per the GM's own measure, says reward him.

recommendations.summary: The rest of the young core is getting the games it has earned.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 39 pts, Nash 26, Chlup 15 in 18 and the D trio all play; Smirnov's scratch is earned, Safronov is a healthy blue-line waiting list, not a snub.

recommendations.summary: Keep giving Chlup (0.62→1.40, 13.0 MPG) and Eminger (0.35→1.20, 20.4 MPG) more of the game — both earned it this window.
recommendations.rationale: Both young players doubled production while their minutes rose, the opposite of a kid being carried. Feed them.

recommendations.summary: Flag Mogilny (35, 1.62→0.75 while minutes rose 16.9→18.5) as a fading piece and start planning the top six around him.
recommendations.rationale: Playing more and producing half as much is the clearest age signal on the roster; no roster move to make today, but the plan should protect against it.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's production inched up (0.43→0.80) but his minutes fell 9.1→8.4 — he is neither developing nor being given the chance.
recommendations.rationale: A 0.80 ppg on shrinking minutes is too thin to call progress; if we intend him to grow he needs the game, if not he is occupying a spot.

recommendations.summary: No one needs more or less of the game for morale; the room is steady and high.
recommendations.rationale: Every dressed player sits at 88 morale or better and unchanged except Chistov (+2) and Roberts/Richards (+3). Spezza at 88 on 9.0 minutes is producing and not slipping, so he stays. Aebischer at 80 is a scratched backup goalie and a roster matter, not a minutes fix.

recommendations.summary: Each unit carries the role it was set for; L1 is the right home for our only faceoff man, checker and scorer.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has checking 77/88 and scoring 86/99, the PP carries Gaborik's 99 shooter on both units, and L4 is a development line that sat empty of a checking role by design.

recommendations.summary: We have one centre above 72 on the draw — Sundin at 86 — and the fourth line sits at 52/52, so we lose the faceoff on three lines every game.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 75 is the only other competent draw man and Richards 72 is a third-liner; no shuffle puts a second 80-plus faceoff centre on the ice.

recommendations.summary: Roster top toughness is Roberts 70 — nothing on the club finishes a check — and the four usable checkers all live on L1 or the penalty kill.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 78 checking is scratched and still not enough depth to build a second shutdown pair, which is why Gaborik ends up on K1.

recommendations.summary: Keep the lineup and Belfour as is for NYR.
recommendations.rationale: NYR leak 3.70 goals per game against our 7.40, and Roberts and Fischer already form the shutdown answer to Lindros' line; no unit change is warranted.

recommendations.summary: McCabe is out tonight; Fischer carries the top pair against Lindros, whoever fills the left side.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe returns 2004-12-15 so this is a one-game cover; no dressed left-defenceman has his CHKG 82, so Fischer (CHKG 87) must anchor that pair tonight.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on L4 now — he is the only internal answer to a lineup with zero 80+ toughness.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker sits not lined with 3 GP but carries 83 CHKG, the third-best checking grade on the club; the roster has no 80+ toughness and the coach flagged him Dec 7. This costs nothing and closes the missing role.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Chara at the deadline: 92 TOUG, 93 CHKG at 27 fixes both the toughness hole and the aging checking corps.
recommendations.rationale: He is 84 ovr, $1.7M, one year left; Detroit's first plus Holden was the noted package Dec 7. At 27 he replaces Roberts 38 and Svehla 35 with the same job at a decade younger.

recommendations.summary: Acquire a centre who wins draws — Sundin 90 is the only man over 80 and Richards 70 is not a playoff answer.
recommendations.rationale: The coach named this Dec 7; no internal move changes the number. This is the one gap that only an acquisition closes, and it needs a name and price before the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Checking is covered only by 35- and 38-year-olds; Chara is the bridge to next season, not a luxury.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 86 at 38 and Svehla 83 at 35 (not lined) carry the role; without Chara the checking corps ages out together exactly as the contracts cluster in summer.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik, Richards and Kaberle on 5-6 year deals now, before the 17-contract summer cluster hits.
recommendations.rationale: All three are 26 or under, productive and expiring in the same summer as 14 others; locking them long now stops their price ratcheting and staggers the next renewal wave.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Svehla, Renberg or Roberts beyond a cheap 1-2 years; let them walk and keep Belfour's decision to the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: They are $8.3M of expiring 34-and-over money that frees room for the young locks, and none is producing enough at 35-38 to justify a term.

recommendations.summary: Hold the Detroit first-round pick and spend it only on a faceoff centre or toughness target that survives three seasons, never on a rental.
recommendations.rationale: The first is the club's only premium asset and the standing holes are long-term ones; the expiring 80-and-over players like Belfour are cheaper in-game currency for deadline needs.

recommendations.summary: At the deadline, buy a centre who wins faceoffs — only Sundin is at 86 — with a first or second round pick, preferring a young player with potential over a rental.
recommendations.rationale: Contending at 21-5-0 and 46 points, the Coach names the draw gap as the roster's one true positional hole and it costs a first or second to fill.

recommendations.summary: If Svehla clears 80 overall by March, move him before expiry for a pick rather than pay a 35-year-old $3.6M into decline.
recommendations.rationale: The above-80 expiring asset trades for a pick, and Eminger (21) and Colaiacovo (21) are the blueline's future, not a 35-year-old at $3.6M.

recommendations.summary: Keep Belfour through the playoff run, then offer a reduced two-year deal at $3.5-4M; if he refuses, Tellqvist (25, $0.8M) starts and Aebischer (26, $0.5M) backs him.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39 at $6.5M expiring; the reduced two-year term is the guide's older-player deal and the correct price for a 39-year-old starter.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik (22, $1.1M) on a 5-6 year deal now; yearly re-signing only ratchets his demands.
recommendations.rationale: He is a priority lock at 22; locking him now avoids next summer's price climb.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards (24, $1.0M) on a 5-6 year deal now.
recommendations.rationale: A 24-year-old centre at $1.0M is the club's future down the middle; lock him before term becomes negotiation.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash (20, $1.2M) on a 5-6 year deal now.
recommendations.rationale: 23 points in 26 games on 12.9 minutes is top-six production the Coach wants on more ice; at 20 he is core, not a question.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle (26, $1.9M) on a 5-6 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: A 26-year-old number-one defenceman anchors the young blueline; he is the oldest core lock and the least negotiable one.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Roberts (38, $2.7M); redistribute his 22.0 minutes to Nash and the young before the legs go.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flags 0.50 pts/g on 22.0 mpg at 38; those minutes belong to players who will still be here in three years.

recommendations.proposed: Upshall, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Chistov, Alexeev, Smirnov
recommendations.summary: Re-sign the six young depth pieces on 2-3 years, staggered, then extend the ones who prove it — so the class never hits one shared renewal summer.
recommendations.rationale: Rookie guidance allows long or short; staggered 2-3 keeps an evaluation window and dodges the simultaneous-renewal trap the guide warns about.

recommendations.summary: Holden (26, $1.2M) is the Chara chip; if that deal stalls because OTT sit 8th at 28 points, judge by March whether he earns a short renewal or walks.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa on the playoff line puts the standing Detroit-first-plus-Holden proposal at risk, and Holden's own renewal depends on that deal.

recommendations.summary: If Renberg (32, $2.0M) is contributing at the deadline, give him a two-year deal; if his minutes or production have slid, let him walk with Roberts.
recommendations.rationale: 32 is an older-player term, not a decline; the March reading decides it.

recommendations.summary: One Ottawa negotiation closes both holes: Chara (84 ovr, 92 TOUG, $1.7M, 27) and White (83 ovr, FACE 81, $0.9M) for the DET first plus expiring Holden and a young defender.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa at 10-10-2 on 28 points with 11 expiring contracts is a selling club; Chara replaces Roberts (38) nine years younger and White is our second-best draw man behind Sundin. Deal dies if Ottawa climbs into the race.

recommendations.summary: The term-and-value toughness fix: Jackman (83 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23) has three years at $0.7M, and poor St. Louis (7-15-2, 22 pts) sells him for our second plus expiring Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: A 23-year-old toughness defenceman with three years of term at $0.7M is the DET-first-quality need at a second-round price; keeps the premium pick in pocket and outlives the deadline.

recommendations.summary: The draw fix as a cheap rental: Sillinger (88 ovr, FACE 96, 33, $1.8M expiring) from seller Phoenix (10-14-4, 26 pts) for a second-round pick, never the DET first.
recommendations.rationale: Best faceoff grade in the pool at 96; a 33-year-old expiring centre Phoenix will not re-sign is worth a second to them. Fallback: Conroy (82 ovr, FACE 93, $2.0M expiring) from worst-record Calgary.

recommendations.summary: If no trade lands, dress Tucker (88 TOUG, 83 CHKG, $1.3M) every night as the toughness floor while the trade targets play out.
recommendations.rationale: The noted internal fallback from Dec 7; his 83 CHKG is already the third-best checking grade on the club and closes the worst gap at zero cost.

recommendations.summary: Acquire a tough forward with 80+ toughness — no player on the 32-man roster exceeds 73 in that grade.
recommendations.rationale: Zero rostered skaters at 80+ toughness. Roberts tops out at 73 and is 38. Tucker sits at 70. This is a personnel gap that line changes cannot close.

recommendations.summary: Acquire a centre with faceoff grade above 80 to play behind Sundin — Richards at 70 is a playmaker, not a two-way centre.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 FACE is the only centre above 80. Richards (70 FACE, 24) is the best option but he is a second playmaker. Chlup (75, 18) is a kid. No internal fix exists.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov every game — speed 92, age 23, 12 points in 11 games, and he is being healthy scratched.
recommendations.rationale: 1.09 points per game over 11 games is top-six production from a 23-year-old. The coach flagged this on 2004-12-04. Scratching him risks both development and morale.

recommendations.summary: Understand why Spacek was scratched — playmaking 84 at age 19 — and return him to the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: Coach reports he went from 16 minutes per game to healthy scratch with no injury. 84 playmaking at 19 is a real grade. The club needs a third centre and he is the closest internal option.

recommendations.summary: Goalie coverage is adequate for the current run; no trade needed before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 9-1 with a 2.57 GAA and 0.907 SV% at 39. Aebischer at 26, 10-3, 3.00 GAA, 0.884 SV% is a serviceable backup at $0.50M. The summer problem is Belfour's $6.50M expiring deal, not this season's coverage.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik, Nash, Richards, and Eminger to 5-6 year deals this summer; they carry $4.5M today and 90+ potential.
recommendations.rationale: All four are on one-year deals at $1.0-1.2M with 88-99 potential and top-6 production. A 5-year lock-up at 3x current salary ($12-16M total) is well inside the $29.5M profit. The alternative is a $28.6M mass expiry where the market finds them first.

recommendations.summary: At the deadline, trade Belfour's expiring $6.5M for a first-round pick or a young prospect using the above-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, 50 potential, 10 GP. Aebischer (26, 90 POTE, $0.5M) and Tellqvist (25, 91 POTE, $0.8M) cover the position at $1.3M combined. Freeing $6.5M and converting it into a pick protects the summer by lowering total re-signing cost.

recommendations.summary: Explore trading Mogilny at the deadline while his 39 points still carry value; $5.5M for two more years at age 35-37 is the roster's worst long-term money.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is producing (39 pts in 26 GP) but his contract runs two more seasons. At 37 with 55 potential he has zero trade value and still costs $5.5M. A contending club might send a pick and a young player for a playoff scorer. If no deal materializes, keep him through the contract.

recommendations.summary: Extend Richards on a 5-6 year deal before the deadline to close the centre gap and prevent an expiring asset at his age from walking.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is 24, $1.0M, one year left. The coach flags thinness at centre behind Sundin. Richards is the answer and he is 84 days from free agency.

recommendations.summary: Extend Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal the season ends; at 22 and $1.10M he is the asset the dynasty is built around.
recommendations.rationale: Already flagged in prior notes as a priority lock. Expiring at 22 means another club will start calling at the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Extend Kaberle on a 5-6 year deal; at 26 and $1.90M he is the top-pairing defenceman the team runs on.
recommendations.rationale: Expiring at prime age with no club control beyond this year. A 26-year-old top-4 D on one remaining year is the kind of asset the market will bid against us.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla before the deadline for a pick; at 35 and $3.60M he is not part of the next three years.
recommendations.rationale: 35-year-old defenceman, $3.60M expiring. A contending club that needs a veteran blueliner is a real buyer. Use the above-80 expiring mechanic if available.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts before the deadline for a pick; at 38 and $2.70M his money is better spent elsewhere.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, $2.70M expiring. A veteran left winger with playoff experience has value to a fringe team. Do not let him walk.

recommendations.summary: Move Renberg before the deadline or let him go; at 32 and $2.00M he is replaceable.
recommendations.rationale: 32, $2.00M, expiring. Not a lock for next season. Any late pick is value on a player we will not re-sign.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on 4-5 years; at 20 and $1.20M, with the coach already using him on the penalty kill, he is a core piece.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, $1.20M, already in the lineup for the PK. Lock him before his next contract starts ratcheting.

recommendations.current: Tim Gleason (Eminger), Ty Smith (Colaiacovo), Vitali Smirnov
recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger (21, $1.20M), Colaiacovo (21, $1.10M), and Smirnov (19, $0.40M) on short deals to preserve depth without overcommitting.
recommendations.rationale: Three young players at $0.40M-$1.20M. Short deals keep flexibility; if they develop, extend later. If they bust, no long-term damage.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Holden on 2-3 years; at 26 and $1.20M he is the depth centre the coach says we are missing.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flags thinness at centre. Holden at 26 fills the 3C/4C role. Moving him creates the very gap the coach named.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chistov (21, $1.10M), Upshall (21, $1.20M), and Alexeev (22, $1.10M) on short deals; they are roster candidates, not core, and short deals protect the budget.
recommendations.rationale: Three 21-22 year-olds at $1.10-1.20M. They are either depth or trade pieces. Two years lets us see which.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Todd Bertuzzi (VAN, 95 ovr, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 29, $2.6M, 1yr) for a first-round pick plus a rental or salary filler.
recommendations.rationale: The single best available asset in the league: a 95-overall power forward on a $2.6M expiring deal with the lowest-payroll club in the league ($34.9M). VAN went 0 rounds last spring and will not pay $6M to keep him. He eliminates the toughness gap outright and gives a second scoring winger the roster lacks.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Zdeno Chara (OTT, 84 ovr, 92 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 98 AGGR, 27, $1.7M, 1yr) for a first-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa are 10-10-2 with 11 expiring contracts. Chara at 27 will demand $4-5M next deal; OTT won't pay it. His 98 aggressiveness and 92 toughness make him the physical presence Toronto's blue line has zero of. $1.7M is nothing against $66.97M payroll.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Shane Doan (PHX, 86 ovr, 86 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 28, $2.4M, 1yr) for a first-rounder or second plus a prospect.
recommendations.rationale: Phoenix are 9-13-4 with 14 expiring contracts and only $14.26M profit against $47.81M payroll. They are rebuilding and cannot keep an 86-overall forward at market price. Doan fills toughness on the wing and provides 25+ point scoring. Cross-conference (TOR East, PHX West) removes division objections.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Kyle McLaren (SJ, 82 ovr, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 27, $2.2M, 1yr) for a second-round pick plus depth.
recommendations.rationale: San Jose are 9-11-2 with 14 expiring contracts. McLaren at 27 with 89 toughness and 93 checking is the same profile as Chara but cheaper to acquire. If the club can only get one blue-liner, Chara edges him by 2 overall points, but McLaren is a realistic fallback at a lower ask.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jason Arnott (DAL, 85 ovr, 87 TOUG, 80 CHKG, 30, $3.8M, FA after this year) for a second-rounder plus a cheap prospect.
recommendations.rationale: Arnott fills the centre gap the coach flagged: he is the only available centre combining 85 overall with 87 toughness. Dallas are 15-9-1 but carry $66.88M payroll against $11.47M profit; losing a $3.8M FA for nothing is worse than getting a pick plus a young body. Cross-conference trade removes division-rival concerns.

recommendations.summary: Include Rob Davison (SJ, 79 ovr, 86 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 24, $0.5M, 1yr) as a throw-in when pursuing McLaren from San Jose.
recommendations.rationale: Davison is 24, costs $0.5M, and carries 86 toughness and 90 checking. San Jose would want a young body back; if McLaren is the primary target, Davison at the same club makes the two-for-one structure natural. He is not a standalone trade but a piece that sweetens the package for SJ.

recommendations.current: DET first-round pick + Holden (C, 26, $1.2M, 81 POTE, not lined)
recommendations.proposed: Chara (D, 27, 84 overall, 92 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 98 AGGR, $1.7M, 1 yr)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Zden Chara from Ottawa for Detroit's first-round pick and Holden; fills the blue-line toughness hole at the lowest cost.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa are 10-10-2 with 11 expiring contracts and no path to re-signing Chara at his next-market price of $4-5M. A first-rounder plus Holden gives them a draft asset and a cheap body. We add 92 toughness and 93 checking at the blueline at $1.7M for a full season plus playoffs. Net payroll change: -$1.2M to us, +$2.9M to them (they shed Holden, add nothing beyond the expiring Chara).

recommendations.current: Mogilny (RW, 35, $5.5M, 2 yrs, 39 pts/26 GP) + TOR first-round pick
recommendations.summary: Acquire Todd Bertuzzi from Vancouver for Mogilny and Toronto's own first-round pick; fills the toughness gap and sheds Mogilny's $11M remaining commitment.
recommendations.rationale: Vancouver are 14-8-2 at the lowest payroll ($34.94M) with $21.93M profit. Bertuzzi at $2.6M expiring will demand $5-6M in July and they likely won't pay it. Mogilny is 39 points in 26 games — elite current production that helps VAN win NOW, and the first-rounder cushions the long-term risk of a 35-year-old at $5.5M for two more years. Toronto saves $2.9M this season, sheds $11M of future liability, and gets the best player available who fills the structural toughness hole. Acceptance is uncertain because VAN is contending and may keep Bertuzzi for a playoff push.

recommendations.current: TOR first-round pick + TOR third-round pick
recommendations.summary: Acquire Shane Doan from Phoenix for Toronto's first-round and third-round picks if the Bertuzzi deal does not land; fills the same forward-toughness gap at lower cost.
recommendations.rationale: Phoenix are 9-13-4 with 14 expiring contracts, $47.81M payroll, and only $14.26M profit. They are in a full teardown and will sell Doan before he walks. Two picks for a 28-year-old 86-overall winger with 86 toughness and 91 checking is fair value for a seller. Payroll effect: -$2.4M to Phoenix, +$2.4M to Toronto. Acceptance is likely given their situation.

recommendations.summary: If all three fail, dress Tucker every night — 92 CHKG, 88 TOUG, 29, $1.3M — as the internal toughness band-aid.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker's 92 checking and 88 toughness are the closest things on the roster to what the coverage phase identified as missing. At $1.3M and only 3 games played, he is wasting away on the bench. He does not close the gap to the league's top tough forwards but prevents the structural hole from being exploited every night.

recommendations.summary: Move Koltsov up from the fourth line — he is producing at a point per game on the fourth line and needs to play where he is challenged.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 12 games (1.00 pts/game) at 8.8 minutes on the fourth line. No other fourth-liner is close to that rate. His development is capped by the quality of competition he sees.

recommendations.summary: Give Nash and his line more shifts per game — 23 points in 26 games on 12.9 minutes a night is top-six production on third-line ice.
recommendations.rationale: Nash is at 0.88 points per game at age 20 and playing only 12.9 minutes. He has earned more of the game. Prefer giving the line more ice over breaking it up, per the chemistry principle.

recommendations.summary: Safronov is 23 with POTE 91 and zero games played — he needs to be in the lineup or the GM needs to tell me why he is not.
recommendations.rationale: Three defencemen under 22 are playing regularly (Klesla 26 GP, Eminger 25 GP, Colaiacovo 11 GP). Safronov at 23 with a POTE of 91 and no games is a development asset sitting idle. Either dress him or tell me what I cannot see.

recommendations.summary: Spacek should be back in the lineup — 6 points in 11 games at 16 minutes a night does not justify a scratch.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek was earning 16 minutes a night and posting 0.55 points per game before being scratched. The production supports a roster spot. I cannot see the reason for the scratch, but the scoresheet disagrees with it.

recommendations.summary: Spezza stays on the fourth line until his production earns a move, regardless of his POTE.
recommendations.rationale: 11 points in 23 games on the fourth line is 0.48 per game — solid for that role, but the GM's standing instruction is that production drives the decision, not the scouting number. He moves when the points say so.

recommendations.summary: Chistov's scratch is correct — 4 points in 14 games at 9.5 minutes did not earn another spot.
recommendations.rationale: 0.29 points per game is below what the lineup needs from a forward. The production supports the decision to keep him out.

recommendations.summary: Watch Gaborik's minutes closely — if the drop from 18.8 to 14.0 holds past this week, he needs to be moved to a line that restores his ice.
recommendations.rationale: His season pace is 1.42 pts/g in 26 games but he managed zero in the last 2 and lost 4.8 minutes a game. At 22, a sustained minutes cut on a first-line producer is how development stalls. One data point, but it is the right direction to flag.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is trending up at 18 — 1.00 pts/g recently on rising minutes. Keep feeding him ice and reassess his line assignment in two weeks.
recommendations.rationale: 8 points in 13 games, then 2 in 2, and minutes up from 11.0 to 12.5. Small sample but the direction is right for an 18-year-old getting real minutes.

recommendations.summary: Roberts is 38 and just jumped to 22.0 mpg while his production fell to 0.50 pts/g. The GM should start planning for a minutes redistribution before the legs go.
recommendations.rationale: Season pace was 1.29 pts/g on 16.5 minutes; the last 2 games show 0.50 on 22.0. At 38 the body collects on 22-minute nights. This is not tonight's problem but it is a roster-planning problem.

recommendations.summary: Room is healthy at 14-2 with zero morale movement across the roster; no minutes changes needed.
recommendations.rationale: Every player's morale is unchanged since the last save. Lowest skater is Chlup at 82, who is getting minutes appropriate to his level. Sundin and Mogilny at 88 on 17.1 minutes are marginally under a 90+ band but stable and aging; better kept fresh.

recommendations.summary: Give Koltsov more of the game on the fourth line.
recommendations.rationale: 98 speed is our second-best on the roster. He is at 53 faceoffs and 54 toughness on a unit that has neither, so he needs game experience to grow into a role beyond raw speed.

recommendations.summary: Insert Tucker on L4 in place of the least productive skill forward.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker's 78 checking and 67 toughness raise the L4 mean from 56 to roughly 65 and give Koltsov a physical partner. The line currently has no one above 63 checking. If Tucker is a healthy scratch, he is the only roster fix for the bottom-six checking gap.

recommendations.summary: We need a centre who wins faceoffs. Only Sundin at 86 can.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 72, Chlup at 75, fourth-line centres at 52-53. We lose the draw on three lines every game. This forces our defencemen into coverage situations they should not face. A second reliable draw-winner is the single biggest roster addition this team needs.

recommendations.summary: Keep L1 as is.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 86 faceoffs, Mogilny 88 scoring, Roberts 80 checking and 70 toughness, McCabe and Fischer 81 checking each. Balanced top line that can win draws, score, and handle a top opponent. Nothing on the sheet says change it.

recommendations.summary: Keep K1 as is despite Gaborik on the penalty kill.
recommendations.rationale: Fischer at 81 checking anchors it, Roberts at 80 adds a second body. Gaborik's 85 stamina lets him handle the shift and the game only pulls him for one PK shift per penalty, not the entire period. The unit mean of 75 checking is our best kill and both our top checkers are on it.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour against New Jersey.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour reads 91 overall with morale 95; Aebischer is 84 at morale 80. The hardest matchup we have faced so far goes to the hotter goalie.

recommendations.summary: Take Colaiacovo off the first penalty kill and put McCabe on it against New Jersey's top power-play unit.
recommendations.rationale: NJ's PP has 8 goals on 52 chances, high volume, and Colaiacovo's penalty grade is 55, the lowest on our blue line. McCabe is 89 on penalties, the cleanest option to kill.

recommendations.summary: Leave the four forward lines as they are for this game.
recommendations.rationale: The lines behind a 10-game streak producing 6.9 goals and 1.4 against a night are settled, and New Jersey has no line weak enough to reward breaking up Gaborik's line or the Sundin line. The third line (Nash, Chlup, Upshall) is already our heaviest and rolls to start on their skill line.

recommendations.proposed: Todd Marchant / Alexei Zhamnov / Jozef Stumpel / Yanic Perreault
recommendations.summary: Acquire a top-nine centre at the deadline — Marchant, Zhamnov, Stumpel, or Perreault all carry one-year deals and could be available from non-contending clubs.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is at 27 points in 25 games on 16.8 minutes a night carrying the second line; Spezza (10 pts, 22 GP, 9.4 min) and Chlup (8 pts, 14 GP) are playoff third-liners on paper only. The Coach says this gap cannot be plugged internally.

recommendations.summary: Add a backup goalie before the deadline — a cheap veteran on a one-year deal or a young prospect for a late pick.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39 with CONS 50 and a $6.50M expiring deal; if he goes down in April, Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) and Aebischer (26, $0.50M) are unproven in a playoff series.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year extension immediately at his next available opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: RW, 22 years old, $1.10M salary, expiring. He is the team's best offensive winger and his current pay is near-rookie level; every year he stays at that salary is a gift, and waiting only ratchets his demands.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to a 5-6 year extension at his next opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: C, 24, $1.00M, 27 points in 25 games. Entering his prime on a contract that should not exist at this level. A six-year deal locks a top-two centre into the franchise.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to a 5-6 year extension at his next opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: D, 26, $1.90M expiring. Entering his prime as the top-pairing defenceman; expect the raise to $3.5-4M but the term protects five years of a prime-year #1 D.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to a 4-year extension.
recommendations.rationale: LW, 20, $1.20M. The Coach is trusting him on the first penalty kill at age 20 — that signals a player developing into a two-way contributor. Four years protects the development window without the full star commitment.

recommendations.summary: Keep Belfour through the playoffs, then offer two years at a reduced $3.5-4M salary; move him for a pick if he declines.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50 and POTE 50 say no upside and inconsistency risk. Still elite in core goalie grades (INTE 97, GSH_ 92, GSL_ 92) but paying $6.5M to a 39-year-old on a one-year ratchet is the classic mistake.

recommendations.summary: Offer Roberts a one-year deal at reduced salary, or move him at the deadline if a contender bites.
recommendations.rationale: LW, 38, $2.70M expiring. TOUG 92 and BALA 94 make him valuable in a playoff series, but at 38 there is no future here — one year at a discount or a rental-to-a-buyer for a pick.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Svehla to two years at reduced salary (max $2.5M), or move him before expiry.
recommendations.rationale: D, 35, $3.60M expiring. ENDU 94 and CHKG 92 are still top-pairing numbers but POTE 55 and his age say decline is imminent. Two years caps the risk at one bad season.

recommendations.summary: Do not sell at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: TOR is 18-5-0, first in the East by 3 points, with a +17-point gap to the ninth team. There is no scenario where selling helps this roster reach a Cup.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov every night; he is producing at 1.09 ppg at age 23 with 92 speed.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 11 games is the best points-per-game on the roster among players under 30. Sitting a 23-year-old at 92 speed who is outproducing everyone except Mogilny/Sundin/Gaborik is wasted development and wasted offense.

recommendations.summary: Return Spacek to the lineup immediately — no injury, 84 playmaking, age 19.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flagged this: 16 minutes a game to scratched with no injury. At 19 with 84 playmaking, every night he sits is a development night lost. He is the team's second-best young centre and should be eating minutes on the second or third line.

recommendations.summary: Remove Gaborik from the first penalty kill; his 98 speed and 92 playmaking are misallocated on a defensive unit.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik's value is offense and speed, not checking. Upshall (80 checking, age 21) or Fischer (82 checking, age 24) are better PK fits and both are young enough to develop the role. Cannot verify Nash's grades from the brief but the principle is sound.

recommendations.summary: Acquire a centre with 80+ faceoff (75 minimum) and ideally 80+ checking; cannot be fixed internally.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin (90 FO, age 33) carries the entire faceoff column alone. Richards is 70, Holden is 71. No internal rotation reaches 75. This is the single most impactful trade target: a two-way centre who wins draws and kills a shift addresses both the faceoff crisis and the thin checking column.

recommendations.summary: Toughness (zero at 80+) is a real gap but does not justify a move at 18-5-0 with playoff spot secure; revisit if first-round matchup is physical.
recommendations.rationale: Best toughness on the roster is McCabe 73. No one at 80+. However, the team is 18-5-0 with 40 points in 25 games and no urgency to spend a pick on a role player. If the first-round opponent is a heavy team, a rental enforcer from a non-playoff club could be addressed at the deadline with minimal cost.

recommendations.current: Nash, Gaborik, Richards, Upshall, Alexeev, Colaiacovo, Eminger (all 1yr)
recommendations.proposed: 5-6 year deals for the young core
recommendations.summary: Re-sign the expiring young core to 5-6 year term this summer, before the single-wave renewal ratchets their prices.
recommendations.rationale: 17 contracts expire for $28.60M, and the core (Gaborik 34 pts, Richards 27 pts, Nash 22 pts; Upshall/Colaiacovo/Eminger POTE 99) is in that group on $1.0-1.2M deals. The manual says lock stars on 5-6 years and avoid a same-summer cluster; re-signing early beats paying a career-year price.

recommendations.proposed: acquire a young centre at the deadline
recommendations.summary: At 18-5-0 we are buying, not selling: spend the Detroit first-rounder on a centre we keep, not a rental.
recommendations.rationale: We hold a first-rounder from Detroit plus our own 2nd-5th, and we are 40 points in 25 games — firmly in the race. The manual's deadline rule for a contender is to buy young players with potential over a first or second pick rather than rent and lose the chip.

recommendations.summary: At the deadline, pursue a young top-6 centre with a first or second-round pick; Richards (24, $1.00M) expiring makes this a double-purpose move.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach says we are thin at centre behind Sundin and cannot fix it internally. Richards is also expiring, so a deadline centre is both a playoff add and a succession plan. The Coach's read that internal shuffling cannot solve it is correct — we have no rostered centre aged 23 or under.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Belfour (39, $6.50M) in the summer; if his grade is above 80, try to move him at the deadline for a draft pick rather than lose him for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 39 and $6.50M is the single largest salary on the roster. Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) is the successor at an eighth the cost. The guide's warning about losing good goalies by forgetting to re-sign applies to Tellqvist, not Belfour.

recommendations.summary: Keep Svehla, Roberts, and Renberg for the playoff run at the deadline even though all three are expiring and will not be re-signed.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla (35, $3.60M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), and Renberg (32, $2.00M) are useful depth for a team that is 18-5-0. Moving them for scraps at the deadline weakens the playoff roster; letting them walk in July saves $8.30M/year cleanly.

recommendations.summary: In the summer, sign Gaborik, Nash, Richards, Kaberle, Colaiacovo, and Eminger to 5–6 year deals and Chistov, Alexeev, Upshall, and Smirnov to 3–4 year deals to avoid a renewal cliff in 2010.
recommendations.rationale: Six players aged 19–21 all expire this summer. All six on six-year terms means they all come up again simultaneously — the guide warns about exactly this. Staggering three of them to 3–4 years means we re-evaluate three prospects in 2007 while locking in the other three at rookie-level salaries now.

recommendations.summary: Chara (27, 95 CHK, 94 TOUG, 31 pts/22 GP, $1.70M, 1 yr) fills the toughness gap (nothing above 73 on our roster) and the checking thinness simultaneously, and his 29 MPG gives us a true second top-pair option behind McCabe.
recommendations.rationale: OTT is 8-10-2, 22 pts, with 11 expiring contracts — they are rebuilding and Chara is on an expiring $1.7M deal, making him a first-round-and-a-prospect candidate. We hold a Detroit first plus second through fifth. The toughness column currently tops out at McCabe 73; Chara at 94 is a two-grade-level jump the roster cannot manufacture internally.

recommendations.summary: Avery (24, 93 face, 86 CHK, 88 SPD, $400K, 2 yrs) is the only young faceoff centre in the league who could become a keeper behind Sundin; LA is 6-10-5, 23 pts, out, with 13 expiring deals and Avery dressed at just 12 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 70 faceoffs is our second-line centre and the Coach's flag is correct — the best available on the roster is Holden at 71. Avery at 93 faceoffs, 86 checking, 88 speed, age 24, $400K, two years controlled is the developmental answer. His 3 points in 24 games says he won't fix scoring, but fixing faceoffs and checking was the goal, not replacing Sundin.

recommendations.summary: Marchant (31, 94 face, 96 CHK, 85 SPD, 30 pts/24 GP, $4.88M, 1 yr) is the best available rental centre if we want to win now rather than develop — he wins draws, kills penalties, and scores at a second-line rate.
recommendations.rationale: CBJ is 6-11-1, 25 pts, clearly out, with 8 expiring contracts. Marchant is the single best two-way centre on the board (94/96/30 pts), but at 31 on $4.88M expiring he is a rental for April, not a re-sign target. Pair this interest with Avery — Marchant for now, Avery for later — rather than choosing one.

recommendations.summary: Belanger (27, 97 face, 83 CHK, $700K, expiring, 3 pts/24 GP) is the cheapest faceoff upgrade in the league and would fix every defensive-zone draw outside Sundin's line for $700K and a late-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: LA is 6-10-5, 23 pts, with 13 expiring contracts. At 97 faceoffs and $700K, Belanger is the lowest-cost solution to the faceoff crisis. He won't contribute offensively (3 points, 8 MPG) but he doesn't need to — he wins the draw and gets off the ice. Could be acquired alongside Avery from the same club to consolidate one negotiation.

recommendations.summary: Savard (27, 88 face, 86 SPD, 84 PASS, 24 pts/23 GP, $1.0M, 1 yr) is the most productive faceoff-capable centre on the market and is on the worst team in the league (5-16-1, 13 pts) with 11 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Savard blends production (24 pts) with faceoffs (88) and speed (86) in a way no other available centre does. At $1M he is cheap. ATL is dead last and in full rebuild mode, so the question is whether they value a 27-year-old centre for a first or accept a second-plus-prospect. If they want too much, fall back on Belanger or Avery.

recommendations.summary: Conroy (33, 94 face, 89 CHK, 25 pts/25 GP, $2.0M, 1 yr) is the cheaper Marchant — same faceoff number, half the salary, two years older — a viable centre rental if Marchant's price is too high.
recommendations.rationale: CGY is 9-14-1, 21 pts, with 10 expiring contracts, clearly selling. At $2M he is far more absorbable than Marchant at $4.88M and still carries 94 faceoffs and 89 checking. At 33 he is a one-year rental with no future implications. The backup plan if Marchant and Savard are both too expensive.

recommendations.summary: Doan (28, 93 CHK, 98 TOUG, 88 fig, 16 pts/25 GP, $2.4M, 1 yr) brings the toughness column from a team-best 73 (McCabe) to 98 in one acquisition, at 28 and on an expiring deal from a club at 8-12-4.
recommendations.rationale: PHX is 22 pts, 8-12-4, out of the race, with 14 expiring contracts. Doan's 98 toughness is the highest available on the board by five points (next best is Chris Neil at 94). His faceoffs at 59 mean he plays wing not centre, but at 93 checking and 98 toughness he is a different kind of answer from anyone on our roster. 16 points is low but acceptable for a checking winger.

recommendations.summary: Jackman (23, 90 CHK, 89 TOUG, 15 pts/24 GP, 31 MPG, $700K, 3 yrs) is a young tough defenceman on a long cheap deal — but STL at 7-13-1 may prefer to keep a 23-year-old with three years left.
recommendations.rationale: At 23 with 90 checking, 89 toughness, 31 minutes a night, 15 points, and only $700K for three more years, Jackman is the long-term answer to the checking-thinness problem alongside Fischer (82 at 24). The risk is that rebuilding clubs keep their young defencemen, and STL has 9 expiring deals but may view Jackman as untouchable core.

recommendations.current: Marc Savard (ATL, C, 27, FACE 88, SPEE 86, PASS 84, 24 pts in 23 GP, $1.00M expiring)
recommendations.proposed: DET 1st round pick + Chistov (TOR, LW, 21, POTE 95, SPEE 89, 4 pts in 14 GP, $1.10M expiring) + TOR 3rd round pick
recommendations.summary: Acquire Marc Savard from Atlanta for the Detroit 1st, Chistov, and a 3rd. He is the only faceoff-capable centre producing at a point per game, and his contract term means we re-sign him on a 5-year deal before he tests the market.
recommendations.rationale: Savard's FACE 88 and 24 points in 23 games directly fix the gap the Coach flagged — Richards at FACE 70 cannot play second-line centre in the playoffs. Atlanta is dead last (13 pts, 5-16-1), carries 20 expiring deals worth $19.3M, and their $36.8M payroll against $34.4M revenue makes them cash-flow negative on a winning basis. A 1st + 3rd + a 21-year-old with POTE 95 and SPEE 89 is the package a rebuilding club with no identity should accept for a player they may not re-sign. We give from wing surplus (10 wingers on roster) and dump a non-playing asset. Net payroll effect: -$0.30M to us (give $1.10M, get $1.00M). Acceptance uncertain — Savard's 24 points are real production and ATL may want a top prospect instead.

recommendations.current: Zdeno Chara (OTT, D, 27, CHKG 95, TOUG 94, SPEE 91, 31 pts in 22 GP, $1.70M expiring)
recommendations.proposed: TOR 1st round pick + Klesla (TOR, D, 22, POTE 97, SPEE 88, AGIL 87, 13 pts in 25 GP, $0.90M, 2 yrs)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Zdeno Chara from Ottawa for our own 1st rounder and Klesla. He is the only player in the league who simultaneously fixes the checking thinness and the total absence of toughness (our best TOUG is McCabe at 73).
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa is 8-10-2 (22 points) with 24 expiring contracts worth $32.9M, $42.8M payroll, and no competitive direction. They hold all five of their own picks, so they want players, not picks. Klesla at 22 with POTE 97 and 13 points in 25 games is a franchise blueliner for a rebuilding club. Chara at 27 is their best asset but he is expiring — if they cannot re-sign him, a young top-D plus a 1st is the right return. We retain Fischer (24, CHKG 90), Eminger (POTE 99), and Colaiacovo (POTE 99) behind McCabe and Chara. Net payroll effect: +$0.80M (give $0.90M, get $1.70M). Acceptance uncertain — Ottawa may want to keep Chara as their franchise D regardless of the record.

recommendations.current: Sean Avery (LAK, C, 24, FACE 93, CHKG 86, SPEE 88, 3 pts in 24 GP, $400K, 2 yrs)
recommendations.proposed: Tucker (TOR, LW, 29, CHKG 92, PENA 89, TOUG 88, 1 pt in 3 GP, $1.30M, 2 yrs) + Holden (TOR, C, 26, ACCE 84, 0 GP, $1.20M, 1 yr)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Sean Avery from Los Angeles for two undressed surplus players, saving $2.10M in dead payroll while adding a FACE 93 centre on a cheap two-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: Avery's FACE 93, CHKG 86, SPEE 88 at 24 on $400K for two years is the best contract-value player on the board. His production (3 pts in 24 games, 12 MPG) limits him to a bottom-six role, but that is still a massive upgrade over Richards at FACE 70. LA is rebuilding with 13 expiring deals and would value Tucker's CHKG 92 as a veteran presence on a checking line. We give two players who are not dressed (Tucker 3 GP, Holden 0 GP) — pure surplus. Net payroll effect: -$2.10M to us. Acceptance uncertain — LA may see Avery as part of their young core regardless of his production.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov needs to be dressed every night — 12 points in 11 games at 1.09 ppg is too good to sit out.
recommendations.rationale: He has the best points-per-game on the club (1.09) and is playing 9.3 minutes on the fourth line at 23 years old. Alexeev produces at 0.60 ppg and plays every game. Koltsov is outperforming everyone on his line and playing 44% of the schedule. The fourth line getting more ice is the right decision made today, but he also needs to be scratched never.

recommendations.summary: Spacek went from 16 minutes a game to scratched with no injury — understand why and put him back in.
recommendations.rationale: He played 11 games at 16.0 mpg at age 19 with potential 91, then vanished from the lineup with no injury record. That was his band and he was playing well enough to hold it. Whatever the reason, a 19-year-old centre going from a regular to invisible without a medical explanation needs attention.

recommendations.summary: Chistov stays a healthy scratch — 4 points in 14 games has not earned a lineup spot.
recommendations.rationale: His 95 scouting number is an opinion; his production is 0.29 points per game at 9.5 minutes. He is 21 and healthy but has not shown enough to displace Nash (22 pts, 25 games) or Koltsov (12 pts, 11 games at 1.09 ppg). The potential means give him a look later when a roster spot opens, not now.

recommendations.summary: Chlup's role is right for an 18-year-old — 11 minutes on the third line is fair. Watch the morale at 82.
recommendations.rationale: 14 games, 11.1 mpg, 8 points. For a rookie centre at 18, that's a fair introduction. Morale at 82 is the lowest in the under-23 group and worth monitoring — if it drops further, the line assignment may need adjusting to keep him engaged.

recommendations.summary: Safronov has no path through the current defensive depth and that is the honest read.
recommendations.rationale: Zero games, potential 91, but Klesla (25 GP, 14.7 mpg), Eminger (24 GP, 15.0 mpg) and Colaiacovo back on the second pair at 18.7 mpg all block him. He is not being wasted — he is behind three defencemen who are playing better hockey. If one of them goes down, that changes immediately.

recommendations.summary: Leave every line as is for NYI; the room is stable and nothing needs a minutes fix.
recommendations.rationale: Every player's morale is unchanged (`=`) and the roster sits 80-100, so no good player is under his band with a slipping number and no depth man is over his head. The lowest, Aebischer at 80, is our backup goalie at 13 starts behind Belfour (56.0 mpg) — a role/results matter, not something a line change moves.

recommendations.summary: Take Gaborik off the first penalty kill and put Nash on it in his place.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik is a 92-scoring, 98-speed winger; the first kill needs checking (it sits at a 77 mean and Roberts 86/Fischer already do that). Nash is the checking body on the third line (line checking mean 79) and is already dressed, so this is a special-teams-only swap with no even-strength cost.

recommendations.summary: Leave the first three even-strength lines as they are; they fit their roles.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has a real shutdown D spine (Roberts 86/McCabe 86 checking) around Sundin and Mogilny; L2 is a speed line (Gaborik 98, Afinogenov 96); L3 is the top checking mean at 79. Rebuilding any of them costs chemistry for no role gain.

recommendations.summary: We are thin at centre behind Sundin and can't fix it by moving people around.
recommendations.rationale: Centres are Sundin 90, then Chlup 75 (18), Richards 70, Holden 71 scratched — no true second-line faceoff man. Against a good faceoff club we lose the draws; that is a roster hole for you, not a lineup arrangement.

recommendations.summary: Keep the four lines and both penalty-kill units exactly as they are for Monday at NYI; do not load the checking surplus.
recommendations.rationale: NYI score 2.50 a night and run the league's worst PP at 2-for-57 (3.5%), so there is no offensive threat to match checkers against; the redress plan waits for a hot-scoring club. We're 18-5 on a ten-game run — break nothing.

recommendations.slot: centre, fourth line or extra forward
recommendations.summary: Put Spacek back on the dressing list — a 19-year-old centre with a 91 scouting number who was playing 16 minutes a night should not be sitting healthy.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek played 11 games at 16.0 mpg with 6 points, now scratched with no injury. Below Sundin we have a faceoff cliff (next best is Chlup at 75), and Spacek was filling it. Brief shows him healthy, 11 GP, no injury row.

recommendations.summary: Carry through on the decision to give the fourth line more shifts — Koltsov is at 1.09 ppg and still only 11 games.
recommendations.rationale: Decision made 2004-12-04 to increase the Spezza/Koltsov/Alexeev line's share. GP hasn't moved from 11 yet. Brief: 12 pts in 11 GP, 9.3 mpg, fourth line, no injury. If GP is still stuck near 11 in a month, this becomes a louder roster ask.

recommendations.summary: Safronov is 23, has zero games, and Colaiacovo's return closes the door — he needs a path somewhere else or he wastes on our roster.
recommendations.rationale: Brief: 0 GP, 0 pts, POTE 91, scratched. Colaiacovo is back on the second pair at 18.7 mpg. No route to ice time for a 23-year-old defenceman behind two established pairs.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov is 19 with a 70 scouting number and zero games — he's not earning a roster spot at this level and the GM should know.
recommendations.rationale: Brief: POTE 70, 0 GP, 0 pts, scratched, morale 100. The lowest scouting number on the U23 list by 20+ points. No production, no games, no case for a roster place.

recommendations.summary: Keep Chlup on the third line at 11 minutes — his morale at 82 is the lowest on the young list but the usage is fair for an 18-year-old and no intervention is needed.
recommendations.rationale: Brief: 14 GP, 56% share, 11.1 mpg, 8 pts, morale 82. At 18 on the third line, that's appropriate development ice. Morale tracks team results and ice-time relative to calibre; keep playing him and let the streak lift it.

recommendations.summary: Move Gaborik off the first penalty kill and dress Tucker to take his spot.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik (scoring 92, speed 98) is an offensive weapon wasting shifts on the kill; Tucker (checking 83) is the right fit and is currently scratched. This was decided on December 4th but hasn't been applied.

recommendations.slot: dressed as seventh defenceman / penalty kill
recommendations.summary: Dress Svehla and add him to both penalty-kill units.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla brings 83 checking and 94 stamina — the best stamina on the roster. He's currently scratched while Gaborik kills penalties. This frees the offensive wingers and gives us two genuine shutdown pairings on the kill.

recommendations.summary: We have no second-line centre who can win faceoffs — this is a trade-deadline problem, not a lineup problem.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 is the only quality draw-taker on the roster. Chlup (75, age 18), Richards (70), and Holden (71) are the rest. Lines two through four get out-muscled at the dot against good centres. No arrangement of this roster closes that gap.

recommendations.summary: The four even-strength lines are well-built for their roles and should not be rearranged.
recommendations.rationale: L1 balances checking (Roberts/Fischer 86), scoring (Mogilny 94) and draws (Sundin 90). L2 is the speed line by design. L3 is two-way with Chlup in the middle. L4 is the speed line. Each has an identity that suits its players.

recommendations.summary: Keep the winning lines exactly as they are for Monday at New York.
recommendations.rationale: New York is 12-10-1, 2.5 goals a game, and their top scorer Yashin is off the lineup entirely; this is a team we beat with our offence (7.5/g, 10 straight wins), not a club that needs a shutdown look. My own rule is to hold the surplus checkers for a hot offensive team, not deploy them here.

recommendations.summary: Leave Gaborik on the first power-play unit and give it ice — their kill is 2-for-57.
recommendations.rationale: New York's penalty kill at 2/57 (3.5%) is the softest edge we'll see; the Gaborik promotion decided this morning already targets exactly this, so no further change is needed beyond using the unit.

recommendations.summary: Belfour starts Monday at New York as planned.
recommendations.rationale: His injury clears for the 5th and he's the higher-equipment starter (INTE 97); this holds the season goalie plan and needs no matchup adjustment against a 2.5-goal team.

recommendations.current: rotation with Aebischer next per Dec 4 promise
recommendations.proposed: Belfour in net Monday at NYI; Aebischer starts Dec 7 vs NJ
recommendations.summary: Belfour starts at NYI on Dec 6; Aebischer keeps his promised start Dec 7 vs NJ
recommendations.rationale: Belfour's injury return date was Dec 5 and has passed; he is cleanly our best (2.57 GAA, .907, 3 SO). The Aebischer promise stands for the first game after this one.

recommendations.current: PP1: Sundin, Roberts, Mogilny, McCabe, Kaberle; Gaborik on PP2
recommendations.proposed: PP1: Gaborik in over Mogilny; Mogilny drops to PP2
recommendations.summary: Gaborik to the first power-play unit, over Mogilny
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik leads the club with 34 points and should take the majority of power-play chances. Mogilny is a week back from a knock. This was decided Dec 4; the current unit still shows it unmade.

recommendations.current: Koltsov: 12 pts in 11 GP (1.09/game), healthy, 9.3 mpg on the fourth line
recommendations.proposed: Give the fourth line more of the game vs NYI's bottom pairs; keep all four lines as they are
recommendations.summary: Roll the Spezza/Koltsov/Alexeev line more tonight; no line shuffles
recommendations.rationale: No injury row explains Koltsov's low GP — this is usage, not health. At 1.09 points a game he has earned more ice; usage is the smaller intervention than breaking up a ten-game-winning line combo.

recommendations.summary: All four even-strength lines and both penalty kills unchanged vs NYI
recommendations.rationale: Ten straight wins, 18 goals allowed in ten games (q36). NYI score 2.5 a night (q37); their checking centre Bates suits Richards on line two without a specialist matchup. Chemistry beats tinkering on the eve of a road game against a cold offence. Shutdown surplus (Tucker, Svehla) stays benched one more night — speed beats smothering at 2.5 goals a night.

recommendations.current: Chistov (21) not dressing, 4 pts in 14 GP; Spacek (19) not dressing since 11 GP at 16 mpg; both healthy
recommendations.proposed: Hold the decision through the NYI/NJ/PIT stretch; reinstate at the first sign of a sag or injury on the top nine
recommendations.summary: Chistov and Spacek remain healthy scratches; first in if anyone sags

Smaller tool first: more of the game if it clicks, move it if it doesn't.

Their kill runs Bates and Mapletoft — our top nine has the matchup against their second penalty-kill pair without touching the order.

recommendations.current: Nine U23s dressed with lines; Smirnov, Safronov, Spacek, Chistov out

recommendations.rationale: Every one of them is dressed with a line and 22 to 25 games except Chlup and Colaiacovo, whose missed games are injuries with return dates of Dec 3 and Dec 1 — both back now. Chlup at 11.1 a night on the third line at 18 is the right dose; his morale of 82 is the one number to watch, not to act on. Colaiacovo at 18.7 on the second pair plus first kill is a young defenceman fully trusted. Smirnov and Safronov have earned zero games on what I can see — scratch is correct for them, and Safronov at 23 and shelved is a roster-plan question for you, not a lineup one. Spacek came off the dressing list at 16.0 a night with nothing in the injury column; I want to know what changed before I plan around him.

recommendations.current: Chlup back from injury at 11.1 minutes a game, morale 82

Morale moves with results and ice time, and he has just missed a stretch through injury; the fastest way to put him back where the rest of the room sits is to give him his shifts back. Koltsov at 9.3 a night with 1.09 points a game is the second name here — if the fourth line draws fewings he should see more, not less. Inference, not measurement: I read this from line, games and morale, there is no shift chart.

Koltsov at 95 despite a scratch-heavy schedule says the room trusts the plan. No structural worry — the winning is doing the work.

L1 checks to a 79 mean behind Roberts at 90 checking; L2 is a scoring line and has four of our top-five shot grades on it (q49); L3 is a real grinding middle unit at 79 checking mean; L4 is the deliberate speed line, whose 32% faceoffs (Spezza, q48) we cover with Richards and Upshall on the important draws rather than by moving anyone. K1 runs Fischer and Roberts at 90 checking; K2 works because Upshall checks 87. The one composition move this phase — Gaborik to PP1, shot 92/accuracy 93, second only to Mogilny (q49), replacing McCabe at the point while McCabe keeps the kill — is the Dec 4 decision already recorded, and it is the smaller tool: one unit changes a man, nobody's line partner changes.

Their PP is the league's worst at 2-for-57, 3.5% of thirty clubs (q50), against our 3 short-handed goals against all season (q51) — special teams is free ice for us. Scatchard (FACE 84, TOUG 85) eats an 18-year-old on the dot, so Richards covers him, not Chlup. But their replacement centre Bates (FACE 94, CHKG 83) is a real first-line centre — correction to my morning read; I won't sell them short.

The smaller tool — more of the game to the top nine against their second kill and third pair — does what a composition change would, without breaking chemistry. No change is the recommendation.

Caveat: first game back, and this data carries no workload history beyond season totals — this is trust in results, not load management.

The scratches are either blocked by a full healthy group (Spacek 6 pts in 11, Safronov behind six working D) or not producing (Chistov 4 pts in 14, Smirnov zero games with the lowest ceiling of the group). Dressing a scratch tonight means benching a productive forward, and the ceiling alone does not buy a spot.

The shutdown surplus only becomes a line decision when an injury opens a slot.

Usage can: the line's speed (Koltsov 92) is real and the checking is not, so stop asking it for what it doesn't have. Zero chemistry cost — no one moves.

recommendations.current: Centres: Sundin (draws 90), Chlup (75, is 18), Richards (70), Spezza (55), Holden (71, scratched)

Our bottom-two centres will lose the majority of draws against any competent centre and no lineup arrangement fixes that. It is a roster problem, not an arrangement problem — we already carry a surplus of checking, so the ask is specifically a centre who can win a draw, not more grit.

DiPietro (3.57) and Snow (4.00) give nothing that forces a personnel answer. The risk in this game is our own let-down spot, not their roster. Zero chemistry cost.
